notes.zh: 作者自述：A quiet marbling bench seen from above: a shallow tray of paper-coloured water set in a dark wooden rim, lit by a soft band of morning light. On load seven drops of indigo, ox-gall, vermilion, celadon and ochre swell one after another into two sets of nested rings that press against each other, and a five-tine comb then draws itself across them, leaving feathered chevrons. The viewer keeps working the same water: every new drop shoves the existing bands outward, every drag pulls sharp feathers through them, and the fan stirs the whole surface in one slow gyre. Type stays tiny and deliberate, on a torn paper slip and a hanging vertical colophon strip stamped with the red seal of the invented Ukigumo Workshop. The tools are drawn objects resting on the wood. Pulling a print is the reward: a sheet unrolls over the water, takes the ink, turns over and flies to the drying rack, leaving a pale ghost behind for the next layer.

tags: - Mathematical marbling on Canvas 2D: every drop is a closed polyline displaced by the area-preserving ink-drop formula, applied incrementally so rings swell smoothly - Tine strokes with exponential falloff around the moving stroke segment, single for the stylus and five parallel tines for the comb, stepped in small increments to avoid folds - Divergence-free curl field (stream function with a main gyre and a counter-eddy) for the fan - Adaptive polyline resampling: stretched segments are split and crowded vertices merged, with a global vertex budget - Procedural caustic light computed per pixel on a low-resolution canvas and upscaled over the ink - Procedurally generated paper grain and fibres, multiplied over the water - Layered ghost rendering: printed ink is redrawn to an offscreen layer and composited at low alpha beneath fresh ink - Prints rendered to their own canvases, mirrored, with a procedurally deckled edge, paper speckle, fibres and a drawn red chop - Scripted print choreography with custom cubic-bezier easings: unrolling clip with a shrinking paper roll, soak-through, turn-over, arcing flight and FLIP landing in the rack - Inline SVG tools (ceramic bowls, bamboo stylus, comb, uchiwa fan, paper stack, skimming strip, brass bowl) with gradients and layered drop shadows - Hand-roughened SVG seal using turbulence displacement and a knocked-out text mask - Vertical writing mode colophon, torn-edge paper slip via clip-path, wood grain from layered repeating gradients, soft inner tray shadow - Small synthesised sounds (water plink, paper swish) through Web Audio, created only after the viewer switches sound on

notes.zh: 作者自述：A dark terminal hall with one object in it: an enamel-framed Solari board for an airship aerodrome that never existed. The page opens on blank flaps; within three seconds a wave of clattering characters rolls from the top-left to the bottom-right and resolves into a full schedule of airships whose times are anchored to the viewer's own clock. From then on the board lives by itself: the flap clock ticks every second, statuses creep from ON TIME through GAS CHECK and BALLASTING to BOARDING and DEPARTED, rows expire and the whole board shuffles up in another cascade, a yellow dot-matrix notice crawls along the bottom with deadpan announcements, and a windsock below drifts with an invented wind. Brass hardware on the frame (a toggle switch for the clatter, a pull lever, a maker's plate) invites touching, and every row opens into a small flap-built manifest with its captain, gas and a purser's remark.

tags: - Split-flap engine drawn on per-field canvases: pre-rendered sprite sheets for every character, size and colour, with time-based fold animation (foreshortening, widening toward the viewer, darkening front face, lit back face, cast shadow, bounce on the final flap) - Forward-only drum cycling with left-to-right, top-to-bottom stagger to produce the cascade wave - Device-pixel-ratio aware canvases (capped at 2) with dirty-cell redraws only - Flap faces with top-light gradient, hairline split, hinge shadow and side pins painted procedurally - Hand-encoded 5×7 dot-matrix font rendered as glowing dots over an unlit lattice, scrolled in whole-dot steps - Brushed-enamel frame, rivets, brass plate, toggle switch and lever built from layered CSS gradients and shadows - Inline SVG airship pictogram, animated windsock (procedural segmented path), compass dial and barograph - Deterministic hash-based schedule and smooth pseudo-weather computed from the real clock - Web Audio filtered-noise ticks, rate-limited to one burst per frame and scaled by the number of flaps turning - Spring and glide cubic-bezier easings for the switch, lever, chips, compass needle and expanding detail strip - SVG turbulence grain overlay and warm overhead light on the page - Responsive cell sizing computed from the board width, with three column layouts

notes.zh: 作者自述：A long-read feature from the invented magazine Crumb Quarterly, No. 14, laid out like a Sunday supplement crossed with a draughtsman's sheet: flour-coloured paper with grain and stray crumbs, a towering Didone headline with a swashed italic "of a", a drop cap, small-caps captions and monospaced measurements. A hand-drawn croissant sits on the title spread; below it, five chapters pair Odile Marchetti's wry essay in the left column with a sticky technical figure on the right that is driven by the reader's scroll. Butter is posted into an envelope of dough, a slab folds in thirds while a counter ticks 1, 3, 9, 27, a triangle winds into a spiral in plan and elevation, and finally the cross-section proofs and bakes: butter lines open into a honeycomb of alveoli, the outline swells by forty percent, the crust browns, steam escapes and a thermometer climbs to 200 °C. The piece closes with tasting notes and a troubleshooting table of the author's own mistakes.

tags: - Paper grain from an SVG feTurbulence filter laid over the whole page at low opacity with multiply blending - Procedurally scattered crumbs and flour dust drawn as tiny irregular seeded polygons and dots - Whole croissant built in SVG from seven overlapping crescent segments with per-segment gradients, tuck shadows and dashed flaky stroke marks - Cross-section modelled as a parametric spiral: about 150 butter cells laid along 12.5 turns, each a path that morphs from a flat butter band into a tapered air cell - Layered sine noise on the spiral, a swelling dome outline with a flattened base, and colour interpolation from pale dough to deep gold - Steam wisps as dashed paths animated with stroke-dashoffset; thermometer mercury and pointer tied to scroll - Letter-fold elevation with hinged thirds rotating in SVG, a travelling rolling pin and stripes that triple each turn - Triangle-to-spiral figure with an Archimedean spiral in elevation, stepped tiers in plan and dashed projection lines between the two views - Envelope figure with flaps folding by mirrored scaling about their fold lines - SVG labels held at a constant on-screen size at every figure scale, with dimension lines, hatching and leader lines - Margin notes with thin leader lines and end dots reaching toward the diagram column - Clip-path wipes for headlines and the pull quote, sprung entrance of the croissant segments, a drawn swash under the italic - Spring physics for the torn croissant ends and gravity, bounce and rest for the crumbs - Sticky figure column on desktop, sticky figure header band on phones; stacked troubleshooting cards on small screens

notes.zh: 作者自述：A night sea in near-black ink strokes, a red-banded lighthouse on its rock, and one heavy, warm beam that is the whole game. The page opens on darkness with the title lettered across the water in tall capitals that can only be read where the slowly turning lamp falls on them. Lighting the lamp starts a four-minute night from 21:00 to 05:00: trawlers, schooners and steamers come out of the dark edges with only a lantern to show for themselves, steering for the harbour mouth, and they will avoid only the rocks the viewer has held the beam on. Everything outside the cone is guesswork and foam glints; everything inside it turns to true colour, with gold wave-crests, sparkling motes, lit sails and long shadows thrown away from the tower. Fog banks swallow the beam, a storm brings rain and swell, and at the end the sea pales to dawn and the whole reef stands revealed. Beside the sea runs the keeper's ledger, where the hour, three lanterns for remaining chances and every arrival and wreck are written in Georgia italic as they happen; the night closes on the finished log page with the keeper's own verdict on the watch.

tags: - Full-bleed Canvas 2D scene with device-pixel-ratio handling (capped at 2) and a pre-rendered background of soft deeper-water bands and vignette - Three-layer light compositing: a dark scene, a separately drawn "true colour" lit scene, and a half-resolution beam mask used both as a destination-in matte for the lit scene and as an additive volumetric glow - Soft-edged cone built from fourteen nested radial-gradient wedges plus thin shimmering lens shafts and an omnidirectional lamp halo - Shadows cut out of the beam mask with destination-out gradients: long diverging shadows behind ships, short ones behind rocks, wide soft ones behind fog banks - World-space motes and rain streaks that only light up when the cone passes over them - Hand-drawn sea of several hundred drifting quadratic and bezier wave strokes in rows, with gold highlight strokes that appear only in the light and swell that grows in the storm - Procedural jagged rock silhouettes with animated elliptical foam rings, self-drawing dashed reveal outlines and fading name labels - Vector ship silhouettes (trawler, gaff schooner, steamer) drawn in two palettes, with lantern glow, reflection, wake trails, funnel smoke and a break-in-two sinking animation - Title lettering drawn glyph by glyph, vertically stretched and letterspaced, existing mainly in the lit layer so the beam reveals it, with a per-letter afterglow - Lens flare (radial bloom, anamorphic streak, starburst rays) driven by the beam's angle to the viewer and its turning speed - Red distress flare with rising trail and wide additive glow, screen shake, storm lightning that silhouettes the reef - Dawn grading that lerps the whole scene toward #3B5368 with a pale band at the top of the sea - Paper ledger UI in CSS: generated grain texture, ruled lines, red margin rules, punched holes, SVG hurricane-lantern icons with flickering flames, entries wiped in as if written - End page with spring-eased entrance, ruled scrollable log, signature flourish and circular SVG text-on-path stamp - Web Audio synthesis: filtered brown-noise sea with slow swell, band-passed rain, inharmonic-partial bell, low sawtooth horn, rumbling thunder

notes.zh: 作者自述：A ten-inch ivory celluloid slide rule by the fictional makers Halloran & Voss lies on pale green-grey drafting paper, pushed in from the left before its scales engrave themselves in a left-to-right wipe and the glass cursor glides to 1. Every tick on K, A, B, CI, C, D and L is placed by logarithm, so the instrument genuinely computes: drag the slide and cursor and a strip of ruled notepaper reports the seven values under the red hairline and says in plain words what the setting works out. Index tabs on the notepaper run guided lessons in which the parts move with mechanical ease while blue pencil notes and dotted arrows write themselves on and the answer is ringed in red pencil. Below, a pencil sketch on the table restates the same setting as two hatched lengths added along a logarithmic line, next to a folded instruction leaflet that explains why it works and how to read a scale.

tags: - Inline SVG instrument with all tick marks and numerals generated from log10, graded long/medium/short with finer subdivisions near 1 than near 10 - Stock, slide, cursor and scale engraving split into stacked SVG layers moved by GPU-composited transforms for smooth dragging - Engraving wipe done with paired counter-translating clip wrappers; entrance push with a custom deceleration curve - Custom motion engine: cubic-bezier(.3,0,.2,1) tweens with a small overshoot and damped settle, drag momentum with exponential friction and sprung soft end stops - Procedural celluloid grain streaks, brass braces with slotted screws, glass cursor with highlight streaks, tinted edges and a soft shadow - Self-drawing annotations: dotted arrows popping in dot by dot, notes revealed with a writing wipe, hand-wobbled red pencil loops drawn by stroke-dashoffset - Drafting-table surface from layered CSS gradients (5 mm and 25 mm grid), pencilled centre line, dimension line and construction marks - Notepaper readout with ruled lines, margin line and punched holes; brass index tabs; folded leaflet with a crease, drop cap and computed "how to read a scale" inset - Live hatched-bar pencil diagram of log a + log b = log ab on a two-decade line - Phone layout with a zoomed, horizontally panning rule and a draggable mini-map of the whole instrument - Reduced-motion mode: no entrance, stepwise jumps with highlighted parts, notes appear without animation

notes.zh: 作者自述：A loud, flat-colour Memphis-Milano landing page for an invented hot sauce made by two cousins in a bus garage. Six colour fields (yellow, pink, teal, terrazzo cream, lava red, yellow) are separated by thick black rules and scrolling marquee strips; every block is strewn with outlined squiggles, triangles, dotted circles and striped slabs that slap on like stickers and then jitter on stepped loops. The wordmark is set letter by letter, each glyph rotated, outlined and hard-shadowed, next to a squat wax-capped flask with a smiling volcano on its label. The centrepiece is a chili-shaped thermometer: dragging its little face from 1 to 10 heats the whole page (faster jitter, wobbling sweating headlines, a rattling cap, steam at the edges, colour fields flipping to red and black) until the bottle blows its cap, confetti-lava rains across the viewport, a starburst shouts "¡AY!" and the slider springs back down on its own. Trading-card sauces, sauce-able pairings, a wonky origin note and an order pad that gets rubber-stamped round it out, all in a funny bilingual voice.

tags: - Inline SVG illustration throughout: flask with clipped gradient sauce, wave and bubbles; three volcano mascots; food icons; bus; chili thermometer - SVG symbol library of Memphis shapes with offset black copies for hard drop shadows, plus dot, stripe and terrazzo patterns - Per-letter display type: individually rotated and offset spans with text stroke, paint-order and hard offset text shadows; wordmark fitted to its column by measurement - Section colours driven by custom properties that flip block by block to red and black at heat 8 and 9, using stepped (not eased) colour transitions - Heat expressed through CSS variables feeding keyframes: jitter amplitude and period, letter wobble, bottle shake and cap rattle all scale from one slider value - Sweat droplets drawn in SVG sliding down letters in three tiers; steam squiggles rising along the viewport edges - Canvas 2D eruption: ballistic particles (triangles, discs, slabs, half-moons, drops, squiggles) with gravity, wall, ceiling and floor bounces, outlined with hard shadows, each aimed to land across the full width - Damped spring simulation returning the slider to rest after the eruption - Sticker-slap entrances with 40ms stagger and springy cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1) pops; bottle drop with squash-and-stretch bounce - 3D card tilt with a hard shadow that leans the opposite way; buttons that press down into their shadow - Rubber-stamp animation roughened with an SVG turbulence displacement filter - Chili-shaped SVG cursor on desktop; reduced-motion variant with a static composition that still recolours

title.zh: Core 7B — Eight Hundred Metres of Winter
title.en: Core 7B — Eight Hundred Metres of Winter

notes.zh: 作者自述：A white, laboratory-quiet logging sheet built around a single continuous ice core. The reader scrolls from a line-art drill tower and summit camp at the snow surface down through 800 metres of procedurally generated ice: snowy, visibly banded firn; bubbly ice; a fractured brittle zone; glass-clear clathrate ice; dusty ice-age ice; gravel-laden basal ice; and finally brown bedrock. An enormous hairline depth numeral in the margin counts every tenth of a metre against an orange reading line, with an estimated age beneath it, while annotation cards and field-log entries by Dr. Ingrid Solheim-Okafor are pinned to exact depths by leader lines that draw themselves. Three live traces, a thin-section light-box and a depth minimap stay in view; the page itself cools slightly with depth. Any point of the core can be cut: a disc slides out, turns face-on and lands in the light-box as a mosaic of crystal grains under rotating crossed polarisers, while the air released from the cut bubbles up the page.

tags: - Canvas core rendered in cached tiles from a depth-to-age model: per-row annual layering that thins with depth, firn grain, bubbles that shrink and elongate, dust and ash bands, a melt layer, fractures, basal debris and bedrock - Column-wise warp that sags every layer into an arc, plus source-atop side shading and a specular strip, so the flat strata read as a cylinder - Custom hairline numerals drawn as SVG stroke paths for the giant depth counter - Voronoi crystal mosaic computed per sample (best-candidate sites, grid-accelerated nearest and second-nearest search, domain-warped boundaries) and recoloured every frame from each grain's extinction angle under a rotating polariser - Thin-section flight animated with the Web Animations API: an edge-on disc slides out of the core, opens to a circle and scales into the light-box - Rising, wobbling, popping bubbles as individually keyframed elements - Leader lines, card rules and text revealed by stroke-dash drawing and clip-path wipes rather than fades - SVG line-art drill tower and camp that draw themselves, followed by the core extruding downward - Three strip charts generated from smooth value noise, with the travelled part inked and a cursor following the scroll - Minimap strip sampled from the same core colour model, with ash bands and sample marks - Page background colour interpolated cooler with depth through a CSS custom property - Optional synthesized sound (filtered noise saw tick, pitched bubble pops)

notes.zh: 作者自述：A hushed, single-lamp mineral gallery for seven specimens that cannot exist. A brass-framed vitrine holds one real-time raymarched crystal floating above a plum velvet plinth, lit by a lamp that slowly orbits so highlights slide from facet to facet; beside it hangs an ivory museum label set in Didot-style italics with a brass catalogue number, a small property table and a paragraph of deadpan curatorial fiction, and below runs a brass rail of seven numbered crystal-habit silhouettes. The page opens in darkness and the lamp warms up over a second and a half. Changing specimen dissolves the crystal facet by facet into glints while a reflection sweeps across the case glass, then the next mineral resolves as the label re-sets itself letter by letter in glowing brass. Switching the lamp to ultraviolet drops the room into violet, makes every mineral fluoresce in a colour it has no business being, and reveals one extra line on the label written in fluorescent ink.

tags: - WebGL fragment-shader raymarching of signed-distance crystals built from plane intersections: truncated octahedron, hexagonal prism cluster with pyramid terminations, bladed spray, chamfered rhombohedron, interpenetrating cubes, hexagonal dipyramid, and a smooth-union botryoidal mass - Faceted normals, Fresnel reflection of a procedural studio environment (softboxes plus the moving lamp), refraction with an interior march, one internal bounce on total internal reflection, thickness-based absorption and per-channel dispersion - Edge detection from the distance field for bevel light and spectral edge sparkle; thin-film iridescence for the black specimen; milky scattering with play-of-colour for the opal one - Velvet plinth with nap noise, grazing sheen, gem-tinted soft shadows, ambient occlusion and a brass rim; filmic tone mapping, vignette and dither - Facet-hashed dissolve with timed facet flashes and screen-space four-point glints, paired with a CSS glass-reflection sweep - Ultraviolet mode: violet lamp and environment, per-specimen fluorescent emission with internal zoning, fluorescent spill onto the plinth, restyled label with glowing hidden ink - Adaptive internal resolution driven by measured frame time, capped device pixel ratio, rendering paused when hidden or off-screen - Letter-by-letter brass typeset shimmer using staggered CSS keyframes with custom easing; SVG turbulence paper and film grain; CSS brushed-brass frame with screws - One shared set of facet polygons drawn as SVG both for the rail silhouettes and for the gradient-faceted fallback crystals shown when WebGL is unavailable - Reduced-motion variant: static lamp, no idle rotation, cross-fade transitions, no letter animation

notes.zh: 作者自述：A bright, full-bleed garden pond seen from directly above at midday. The water runs from pale jade shallows at the mossy corner stones through teal to a deep centre, with pebbles on the floor and a slow net of caustic light sliding over everything, fish included. Nine to thirteen koi, each a flexing spine with its own painted pattern (kohaku, showa, ogon, tancho), cruise in bursts and glides, paddle their pectoral fins and drag soft shadows across the floor that lengthen over deeper water. Lily pads drift on tethers, two lotus flowers breathe, maple leaves turn, water striders dart, and now and then a dragonfly and its shadow cross the frame. The page opens in white glare that settles like eyes adjusting to the sun while the fish swim in from the edges. There is nothing to achieve: tap for ripples, hold to feed, and watch the whole pond turn towards one spot.

tags: - Canvas 2D scene with devicePixelRatio capped at 2, paused when the tab is hidden - Koi built from a 14-node towed spine chain with a travelling sine wave whose amplitude follows tail thrust - Body outline from a width profile sampled along the spine, smoothed with midpoint quadratic curves - Per-fish seeded blob patterns defined in spine coordinates, so the markings bend with the body, clipped to the body shape - Paddling pectoral and pelvic fins that fold during a burst, a two-lobed fanning tail with fin rays, edge shading and a wet dorsal sheen - Steering behaviours: wander, separation, edge, stone and lily-pad avoidance, flee, return, pointer following and food seeking with a tangential swirl - Burst-and-glide speed model driving tail-beat frequency - Soft shadows drawn to a quarter-resolution layer and scaled up, offset further in deeper water - Pond floor painted once from a depth field (superellipse falloff plus stone proximity) mapped through the jade, teal and deep ramp, with procedural pebbles - Animated caustics from an iterated-sine turbulence function computed at low resolution, depth-masked and added with lighter compositing - Ripples as concentric highlight and shadow ring pairs with a brighter sunward arc - Procedural stones with speckle, veins, rim light and stippled moss, pre-rendered to an offscreen canvas - Lily pads with notches, veins, water beads and spring-driven bobbing; layered-petal lotus flowers - Maple leaves, water striders with dimple shadows on the floor, and a dragonfly with flickering wings and a displaced shadow - White glare entrance fade; quiet Georgia italic captions with a vertical signature - Optional synthesised sound: filtered noise trickle with randomised sine plips

notes.zh: 作者自述：A white-cube gallery reduced to two values. The visitor arrives at a title wall where enormous condensed capitals are sliced by horizontal hairlines that beat against each other, then walks down through six snap-aligned rooms that alternate between black and white. Each room holds one square work made from nothing but a repeated line, ring, check or spoke laid over a copy of itself: rings that produce sweeping hyperbolas, a checkerboard that swells into a dome, upright stripes that ripple, spokes that bloom into counter-rotating petals, ruled paper that folds into a pleated curtain, and finally a black disc that the viewer stares at until it disappears and leaves a glowing ghost on a blank wall. Signage is tiny, uppercase and widely spaced, with a large roman numeral and a dry wall note per room. The mood is exacting, quiet and slightly dizzying; everything that seems soft, grey or three-dimensional is produced by the viewer's own vision.

tags: - Two repeating-radial-gradient ring fields blended with mix-blend-mode: difference, drifting on sine-eased translate animations to generate moire hyperbolas - Twenty-six nested circular clip layers of a repeating-conic-gradient checkerboard, each scaled by a per-layer custom property along a logarithmic profile to fake a lens - Five phase-shifted stripe layers revealed through diagonal repeating-linear-gradient masks whose position advances with steps() timing - Counter-rotating repeating-conic-gradient spoke fans with different spoke counts in difference mode, split into annulus and disc by a radial mask - Alternately skewed overflow-clipped slices of ruled lines with two line weights to model light and shade on pleats - Pure-CSS twenty-second timer: SVG stroke-dashoffset progress ring, steps() digit strip countdown and step-end visibility keyframes driven by a checkbox - background-clip: text title with two hairline gradients combined by background-blend-mode: difference and a retracting solid cover layer for the entrance sweep - Container query units (cqw) so every pattern scales with its work, and a title sized to its wall - Fixed index in difference blend with scroll-driven view timelines (timeline-scope) and a :target fallback - Checkbox-and-label state machine: paused booster animations switched by :hover and :checked, freeze via animation-play-state - Clip-path wipes and scaleX rule draw with custom cubic-bezier easing instead of opacity fades, keeping the page strictly two-valued - prefers-reduced-motion variant with hand-chosen static frames for every work

notes.zh: 作者自述：A clock that is only a sentence. The viewer's local time is written out in lowercase English and set as a wood-type broadside: every line is measured to its ink and scaled to the full width of the screen, the minute phrase in heavy italic, the whole block packed into a solid rectangle on a single flat field of colour that drifts through twenty-four hand-picked pairs across the day, from aubergine small hours through dawn peach, white-hot noon and terracotta evening back to deep blue. When the minute turns the poster re-typesets itself in place: only the letters that differ roll out and in, and the lines swell or shrink to stay flush with both margins. In the corners, tracked monospace capitals carry the date, year, time zone and day of the year, all in words, while a hairline along the bottom edge counts the seconds. The effect is of a printed sheet that happens to be alive, calm at rest and briefly mechanical once a minute.

tags: - Per-glyph canvas text measurement (advance, kerning pairs, ink bounding boxes) so each line is fitted to its true ink edges, not its advance width - Exhaustive line-break search over every partition of the sentence, scored for how fully the fitted lines fill the stage, the size of the italic key phrase, scale contrast and stability against the previous setting - Lines stacked by measured ascent and descent rather than line-height, with a uniform vertical condense/extend to close the block - Letter slots positioned in em units and re-flowed every frame, so a line stays exactly edge to edge while its letters change width mid-transition - Prefix/suffix letter diff per line and longest-common-subsequence matching between old and new lines, so unchanged letters and lines never move - Staggered letter rolls (30ms apart, cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.2,1.1)) clipped to each line's ink band like an odometer; the same curve solved in script to drive the re-justification - 24 background/ink pairs blended in OKLab by the minute and second, with a contrast floor that steers the ink toward black or white where two hours cross - Slow field/ink inversion on the hour with an italic serif note - Procedurally generated fine paper grain tiled over a flat colour field; no gradients - Phrase generator covering all 1,440 minutes in two registers, plus cardinal and ordinal number writers for the date, year, day of year, time zone offset and scrub distance - Reduced-motion variant: letters cross-fade, layout eases without overshoot, no inversion flash

notes.zh: 作者自述：A wide marsh sky in the last minutes of light: plum-ink overhead sinking through mauve and coral to a pale apricot horizon, a low sun and its broken reflection in a thin strip of water, pylons and poplars tiny on the far bank, and a black reed bed swaying along the bottom edge. Into the empty sky a long ribbon of starlings streams from the right and gathers into a single breathing shape made of thousands of tiny flapping chevrons, lighter where the birds are far and darker where the flock folds over itself, stretching into ribbons and hourglasses and rippling with sudden dark waves when it turns. The viewer's pointer is a peregrine; the flock parts around it, wraps behind it and closes again, and a click sends the falcon into a tucked dive that tears a hole straight through the birds. Left alone, the falcon hunts by itself, the light slowly fails, and the whole flock drains through a narrow neck into the reeds; after a few seconds of stillness a new evening begins. The only words are a tiny italic title, a live count of starlings, a hint that dissolves once the hunt starts, and two quiet controls.

tags: - Boids simulation in typed arrays with a counting-sort uniform spatial grid; separation, alignment and cohesion limited to about seven sampled neighbours - Per-cell sums for a wider neighbourhood heading, centre-of-mass pull and a density-gradient pressure that keeps the flock a spread fabric rather than a clump - Twin roost attractors that drift on slow Lissajous paths and periodically separate, pulling the flock into ribbons and hourglasses - Excitable-medium agitation wave (delay, attenuation, refractory period) passed between neighbours, drawn as briefly thicker, longer strokes - Fake depth from a per-bird z blended with a moving sheet field; four depth bands by stroke width and opacity, each split into calm and agitated batches - Birds as two-stroke chevrons whose wings alternate in length to flap; batched Canvas 2D strokes - Low-resolution density buffer from the grid, bilinearly upscaled as a soft smoke-like shadow where the flock overlaps itself - Procedural dusk painting: four-stop sky gradient, translucent horizontal washes, sun bloom and disc, mirrored water gradient with a broken sun reflection and animated glints, value-noise treeline, lattice pylons with sagging wires, poplars, vignette and baked grain - Long thin clouds built from stretched radial gradients on their own layer, drifting by compositor transform - Two-layer reed bed with quadratic-curve stems, plumes, bulrush heads and leaves swaying on layered sine waves, stirred locally where birds land or erupt - Falcon silhouette drawn from quadratic curves with banking, wingbeat and a tucked stoop pose, plus stoop streak and expanding ring - Evening state machine: slow light fade, funnel descent with a fanning neck, rest, new evening - Adaptive quality (flock size, reed and haze refresh rate), DPR cap, pause when hidden, reduced-motion variant - Web Audio wing rush: looped noise through band-pass and high-pass filters with a flutter LFO, driven by flock speed and fear

notes.zh: 作者自述：A top-down view of a classroom demonstration: a sheet of warm white paper, fibres catching soft daylight, dusted with fourteen thousand black iron slivers. Two red-and-blue bar magnets glide in from opposite edges and the random dust visibly combs itself into the textbook pattern, pulling a dense bridge of filings across the gap between north and south. From there it is a toy: slide, spin and flip the magnets and watch the alignment wave chase them, see tufts of filings cling to the poles and get dragged along leaving swept trails, flick the paper to tidy the lines, bring like poles together to find the pencil-circled null point, and drop a horseshoe or disc magnet, a compass, or a fresh shake of filings from the apparatus tray. A taped typewritten label and a pencilled note are the only words on the sheet.

tags: - Two stacked Canvas 2D layers: a procedurally painted paper (fibre strokes, noise tooth, daylight wash, vignette, printed registration marks and scale bar) and a live layer - Filing simulation in typed arrays: summed softened-monopole field, per-filing lagged axis alignment, gradient-of-field-strength creeping with friction and per-filing stopping thresholds - Batched line rendering in six paths bucketed by dithered field strength and grey variation, with length and weight tied to field strength - Magnets, compass and shaker drawn in code with painted-metal gradients, stamped lettering, bevel highlights and lift-dependent drop shadows - Flip animation by axis scaling with polarity swap at the midpoint and the field strength following the turn - Damped-spring compass needle driven by the local field - Midpoint-integrated streamlines seeded around each pole with arrowheads and a progressive draw-in, in pencil blue - Automatic null-point detection between like poles with a hand-drawn pencil annotation - Outward-travelling tap ring that jitters filings as it passes - Time-based tweens with custom easing for the entrance, tray hand-offs and tray/label choreography in CSS - Web Audio noise hiss mapped to filing motion, off by default - Sleep-when-settled render loop, DPR cap, resize rescaling, reduced-motion variant

notes.zh: 作者自述：A white sheet set like a Swiss mathematics poster: an enormous lowercase grotesk headline runs up the left edge with one word in red-orange, a hairline-framed square field fills the height of the window, and a narrow monospace rail of rules, sliders and tabular figures sits to its right. The field holds every integer up to N as one small square. It opens by drawing all of them as a single black line, reeling that line into a solid black square spiral, and then sieving it from the centre outward behind a red front until only the primes remain, scattered along unmistakable diagonals. Choosing another arrangement sends every dot along its own path, centre first, so the square coils into the Sacks spiral, flares into the polar galaxy, or falls into rows whose columns stripe at widths like 30 and 210. Pointing at any dot produces a black label with its arithmetic and lights the diagonal, curve, column or arm it belongs to in red; zooming in far enough turns the dots into numbered tiles.

tags: - Sieve of Eratosthenes with prefix tables (prime count, twin pairs, widest gap) computed once in typed arrays - Direct pixel plotting of up to 250,000 squares into a Uint32 view of canvas ImageData, with culling and DPR capped at 2 - Per-point staggered morphing with a tabulated cubic-bezier(.65,0,.2,1) ease; unwrapped polar interpolation between the Ulam and Sacks spirals, shortest-arc polar interpolation to and from the (n, n) plot, Cartesian elsewhere - Opening choreography: progressive line draw, wrap into the spiral, radial red sieve front with a grey trailing band - Vector overlays on the same canvas: twin-prime links, Euler's polynomial thread with filled/hollow markers, the highlighted quadratic or residue class, a sprung cursor ring with tick marks - Level-of-detail numerals drawn inside each square once cells are large enough - Anchored exponential zoom smoothing so the point under the cursor stays put - Rotated vertical headline in tight bold grotesk with clip-path wipe entrance; rules that draw in along the rail - Custom sliders, square toggles, inverted radio rows and a live gap histogram built from plain elements - Cross-fade via a snapshot canvas for reduced motion

notes.zh: 作者自述：A slow, bilingual landing page for the invented Parisian house Maison Ombre and its single fragrance, No. 7 — Bibliothèque Brûlée. On warm ivory laid paper, crossed by a drifting casement of pale window-light, an enormous oxblood italic title runs behind one exquisitely drawn flask; the word seen through the glass is bent by it, and the amber-oxblood liquid inside tilts, sloshes, ripples and bubbles as the pointer passes or the flask is tipped. Scrolling carries the same flask into the olfactory pyramid, where its oak cap lifts off and the notes rise from the neck as fine wisps and then evaporate in order, top first, heart next, base lingering, before three quieter movements: a portrait of the perfumer beside a scorched, tea-ringed folio, the object's specifications with a dimensioned elevation and a discreet table of editions, and a one-line request for a sample card that is answered by an envelope closed with a wax seal.

tags: - Flask drawn entirely in inline SVG: eight bevel facets, layered linear gradients for thick glass, gilt collar, charred-oak cap with grain and cracks, paper label with old-style numeral - Liquid surface rebuilt every frame from a spring-damped tilt angle plus a one-dimensional wave simulation that reflects off the walls; a second offset line gives the surface depth - Bubbles spawned by slosh energy that rise, wobble and dimple the surface when they break - Refracted title: a live copy of the second title line clipped to the flask cavity, magnified and offset about the cavity centre and re-registered each frame - Blurred SVG cast shadow and wavering caustic streaks under the flask that lean and brighten with the position of the window-light - Window-light as a skewed, blurred grid of six panes drifting on a slow sine; glass reflections shift with it - Laid-paper texture from two repeating CSS gradients (laid lines and chain lines) - Wisps as pooled SVG paths whose points are advected through a slow sinusoidal flow field, coloured gold, oxblood and soft black for top, heart and base - Scroll-driven choreography with smoothed scroll position and smoothstep easing: flask travel and scale, cap lift, note emergence, tracking and evaporation, hour clock - Title entrance by true letter-spacing closing from wide to set, with per-letter staggered opacity - Scorched folio using feTurbulence and feDisplacementMap for torn edges and cockled lines, a radial scorch gradient and a broken tea ring - Dimensioned line elevation that draws itself with stroke-dashoffset; hairline rules that draw in from the left - Wax seal with turbulence-displaced edge, radial gradients and an embossed SVG monogram, dropped and pressed with spring-like keyframes - Custom gold ring cursor that follows on a spring and swells over interactive elements - Reduced-motion version with a level, still liquid, all notes visible, no wisps and a fixed window-light

notes.zh: 作者自述：A single cathode-ray tube sits in a dark cabinet above an engraved model plate. Everything on its face is light: mint-white beam cores wrapped in green bloom, vertices that burn a little brighter where the beam pauses, and a phosphor that takes a moment to forget what it was shown. The attract screen traces the word DESCENT one stroke at a time while a cratered wireframe moon turns behind it and an autopilot quietly demonstrates a landing below. Starting a mission hands over a small legged module drifting above jagged regolith; the camera eases in to two and a half times scale as the surface approaches, the engine plume fans out and flickers, dust streaks away along the ground in short glowing lines, and the whole tube brightens with the burn. A clean touchdown earns a dry remark from mission control and a harder site; anything else scatters the lander into its component segments, which tumble, bounce and fade while the phosphor remembers their arcs.

tags: - Canvas 2D beam renderer: every segment batched by brightness and stroked as wide glow, medium halo and thin mint core, with extra dots at vertices - Two-layer phosphor model: an additive persistence buffer faded in steps (with a residue-clearing burn pass) under a crisp current-frame pass, so moving objects leave decaying trails - Halation from a quarter-resolution blurred copy of the picture screened back over the tube, plus a throttle-driven glow on the glass - Custom vector stroke font on a 4×6 grid for all on-screen text, including arrows, a multiplication sign and a slashed zero - Sub-pixel beam jitter, occasional brightness flicker and a barrel warp applied per endpoint - Procedural periodic terrain from layered value noise with carved landing pads, a parallax far ridge with hidden-line testing, and a fixed star field - Thrust plume as a randomised fan of lines scaled by throttle and clipped to the ground, with line-particle dust spawned where the exhaust strikes the surface - Crash break-up: each hull segment becomes a tumbling, bouncing rigid line with sparks and an expanding dashed shock ring - Smooth altitude-driven camera zoom from 1× to 2.5× with a horizontal dead zone - Self-drawing title built from the font's stroke order with a beam head and periodic retrace sweep; rotating wireframe moon with latitude, longitude and crater circles and back-face dimming - CSS tube: rounded glass with barrel vignette, blurred window reflection, fine grain, thin bezel and an engraved plate with screws and a power lamp - Web Audio synthesis: filtered-noise engine rumble, triangle-wave warning beeps, noise-and-sine crash

notes.zh: 作者自述：A six-spread stapled zine laid out on a cutting mat, printed in exactly two inks. Everything on the page, from the full-width cover title to the smallest weather icon, exists twice: once on a fluorescent pink plate and once on a teal plate, multiplied together over flecked recycled paper so that overlaps turn a deep violet nobody paid for. The plates never quite agree. As the viewer moves, scrolls or tilts, the pink plate slides a few pixels against the teal one with a soft spring, keylines drift off their fills, halftone screens beat against each other, and a printer's registration target in the corner reports the error and can be dragged to make it much worse or double-clicked to make it, briefly, perfect. Inside that process sits a warm, funny little publication by two damp people and a cat: instructions for taking a spore print (with a cap you can lift to watch one land), five mushrooms described like neighbours, a centrefold of roots and mycelium growing under the fold, letters, a month of rain, and a stamp telling you to pass it on.

As the viewer moves, scrolls or tilts, the pink plate slides a few pixels against the teal one with a soft spring, keylines drift off their fills, halftone screens beat against each other, and a printer's registration target in the corner reports the error and can be dragged to make it much worse or double-clicked to make it, briefly, perfect. Inside that process sits a warm, funny little publication by two damp people and a cat: instructions for taking a spore print (with a cap you can lift to watch one land), five mushrooms described like neighbours, a centrefold of roots and mycelium growing under the fold, letters, a month of rain, and a stamp telling you to pass it on.

tags: - Two stacked SVG plates per illustration (pink and teal) composited with mix-blend-mode: multiply over paper, so overprint produces the third colour - Global registration offset driven by CSS custom properties, added to a different base error on each spread, with spring-damped motion - Ink grain: tiling SVG feTurbulence tiles (fine speckle multiplied by coarse mottling) used as CSS mask images, different for each ink - Recycled paper: thresholded turbulence flecks and stretched-noise fibres as tiled backgrounds - Halftone dot screens and line screens as SVG patterns at different angles per ink (15° and 75° dots, crossed line screens) - Hand-drawn wobble from an feDisplacementMap filter applied identically to both plates - Radial gills drawn with a single dashed, very wide circle stroke squashed into an ellipse - Cover title as SVG text with textLength fitting, pink flat plus teal keyline with screens clipped to the letterforms - HTML headlines doubled with pseudo-elements: pink fill on the moving plate, teal text-stroke keyline on the fixed plate - Canvas spore print: thousands of jittered dots along primary, secondary and tertiary gill rays, revealed from the centre outward - Procedural centrefold: seeded random-walk roots with tapering widths, mycelium links and wandering forks, grown with stroke-dashoffset; rebuilt in portrait proportions on phones - Paste-up blocks with torn tape, crop marks, colour bar, drawn staples and fold shading, scribbled page-number rings - Container-query units so each spread scales like a printed sheet; paper-slap entrance with an overshooting cubic-bezier

title.zh: Plotter No. 2 — Landscapes in One Pen
title.en: Plotter No. 2 — Landscapes in One Pen

notes.zh: 作者自述：A bright, technical bench-top scene: a white A4 sheet lies on a pale grey gridded cutting mat inside a drawn pen plotter with two aluminium rails, a travelling gantry bar, a black carriage with a cable loop and a ballpoint whose red clip is the only warm colour besides the hold button. On load the carriage homes into the corner with a small bump, rules the border and registration crosses, then works through the sky, each ridge from far to near, the lake or pines, and finally letters its own title block. The landscape is a true plot file: every mark on the sheet is an ordered polyline that the pen actually travels, with travel moves, pen lifts, corner slow-downs and ink that is paler when the pen runs fast. The pleasure is in watching tone accumulate as the machine hatches a mountainside in hundreds of quick strokes, while a small LCD reports pen state, coordinates, percentage and time remaining, and a listing on the mat ticks off the layers. Every new sheet is a new seeded composition, and the finished ones pile up in the out tray.

tags: - Seeded procedural landscape: 5–8 ridgelines from layered value noise and ridged noise with a peak envelope - Hidden-line removal with a running per-x horizon, walked front to back, also used to occlude the sun, clouds and the ridges behind the pines - Five hatching generators (slope-wobbling contours, vertical rain dashes, cast-shadow cross-hatching, scree stipple, downhill fall lines) with density falling off with distance - Lake of horizontal dashes whose density mirrors the skyline through a ripple displacement; pines as dense zigzag strokes - Single-stroke vector alphabet defined in the page, used for the plotted title block - Path simplification and greedy nearest-endpoint ordering of each layer to minimise pen-up travel - Motion planner: resampled paths, corner speed limits, forward/backward acceleration passes, trapezoidal travel moves - Incremental ink rendering on an offscreen canvas at capped device pixel ratio: pen-down blobs, speed-dependent opacity, width jitter and minute positional wobble - Canvas-drawn machine: brushed aluminium gradients, steppers, gantry trucks, a sprung cable loop, pen shadow that separates on lift, servo arm and state lamp - CSS-built control panel: brushed faceplate, conic-gradient knurled dial, lever toggle, keycaps, emergency-stop style hold button, reflective LCD with segment bar - Sheet feed animation with eased slide, slight rotation into a peeking stack of earlier plots - Optional stepper sound: two oscillators pitched from the X and Y axis speeds, filtered noise clicks for pen up and down

title.zh: Rhythmus — A Drum Machine in Primary Colours
title.en: Rhythmus — A Drum Machine in Primary Colours

notes.zh: 作者自述：Rhythmus is a poster that happens to be an instrument. On warm, toothy paper a wall of hand-drawn geometric capitals climbs the left edge, and a heavy black bar cuts across the sheet at seventeen degrees with the tempo reversed out of it like a ruler. Six flat-colour shapes balance on and hang from that bar: a blue circle resting on the incline, a red square standing on its edge, a yellow triangle, a black half-disc facing its outlined twin, a thin red mallet on a black pivot, a blue ring. Below, a six-by-sixteen grid repeats the same shapes in miniature as the score. Press the red circle and the composition starts to move: every drum hit is performed by its shape with spring physics, the playhead sweeps the grid, the title letters step along with the bar, and the whole print keeps time. Everything is drawn in code, with slightly ragged printed edges and off-register fills, and the layout re-composes for phones with the stage above a two-page grid.

tags: - Single inline SVG composition built on a rotated "axis" group, so the bar, tempo ruler and all six voices share one tilted coordinate system - Title lettering constructed from stroked bars and arcs (no font dependency), clipped to cap height and rotated to run up the left edge - feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap filters for slightly imperfect printed edges on the title, the bar and the large shapes - Paper tooth from a tiled fractal-noise texture multiplied over the whole sheet - Custom spring integrator (semi-implicit Euler, sub-stepped) driving squash, quarter-turn roll, shiver, clap collision with restitution, mallet strike with bounce, and ring pulse - Geometric contact for the square: its centre lifts by half

(|cos|+|sin|) so it truly rolls over its corner on the bar - Pooled expanding ripple rings with eased radius, thinning stroke and fading opacity - Tempo numerals drawn twice (black, and paper clipped to the bar) so they invert as they swell beyond the bar - Staggered entrance: bar wipe, letters sliding up with overshoot, shapes sliding and rotating in along the axis, grid shapes popping in column by column - Sequencer steps as small inline SVG glyphs with outline and off-register fill layers and overshoot transitions - Web Audio synthesis of six drum voices with a lookahead scheduler, swing, accents and a master compressor - Playhead position interpolated from the audio clock; unit-based layout that scales the whole board to the viewport, with a separate stacked composition for narrow screens

notes.zh: 作者自述：A silent winter night at 69°N, seen from the shore of an invented fjord. The page opens on stars, black mountains and one lit cabin window; then a green curtain of light unrolls from the left and the sky comes alive. Three aurora curtains hang in true perspective: folded ribbons with crisp, bright lower borders, tall rays that shimmer sideways, pale cores and violet upper fringes, the nearest arching overhead while the farthest lies low over the mouth of the sound. Snow on the peaks picks up the green, the water below breaks the whole sky into long trembling streaks, and a thread of smoke rises from the cabin beside a jetty and a moored boat. A small plate of type in the corner names the place and slowly turns the pages of an observer's notebook. The viewer can simply watch, or stir the solar wind and call down a substorm that floods the fjord with light.

tags: - Hand-written WebGL fragment shader on a single full-screen triangle; the entire scene is procedural - Aurora as thin sheets on noise-folded ground-plane ribbons, found by walking each view ray and locating exact sheet crossings, with near-miss handling for folds seen edge-on - Vertical emission profile with a sharp lower border and a variable exponential tail; 1D ray noise at three scales; green-to-violet height colouring with a pale core and soft tone mapping - Hashed star field in three layers with twinkle and aurora dimming, Milky Way band, thin high haze, teal horizon glow, rare meteor with tapered tail - Ridged-noise mountains in four depth layers with snow caps, rock gullies, haze by distance and green rim light - Water built from three mirrored, ripple-displaced samples of the scene with perspective-scaled ripple frequencies, giving vertical glitter streaks - Signed-distance cabin with lit mullioned window, lamplight on snow, chimney smoke thread, warm streak reflection; jetty, moored boat and spruce silhouettes - Entrance choreography driven by per-curtain reveal uniforms; substorm front expanding from the click point - Adaptive internal resolution and sample count, film grain and lens falloff to keep dark gradients smooth - Web Audio wind and crackle synthesised from filtered noise - CSS/SVG fallback scene with masked, blurred gradient curtains and mirrored reflection

title.zh: Drawer 31 — Moths That Were Never Caught
title.en: Drawer 31 — Moths That Were Never Caught

notes.zh: 作者自述：A walnut specimen drawer slides out from under a cabinet rail and fills, moth by moth, with two dozen species that never existed: emperors with ringed eyespots, swept hawk-moths with rose underwings, angular lichen-green geometers, stout owlets and tiny fringed micros, each painted procedurally from a seed, mirrored for symmetry and then slightly damaged the way real specimens are. Rows are grouped under printed genus headers, every pin in a row sits on one line, and beneath each moth is a small tilted label in uneven sepia handwriting. The lining paper is foxed at the corners, the glass carries a faint moving reflection, and the drawer front holds a brass label holder, a cup pull and a small brass switch. To one side a huge Didot numeral and a dry curatorial note explain the collection of E. M. Hollis, who pinned the moths he was sure of and never caught. The experience is quiet and studious: pass a brass magnifier over a specimen to read its scales at three times life size while its typed index card slides out, turn the whole drawer over to see the pale undersides, pull the next drawer, and eventually discover that one specimen in each drawer is still alive.

tags: - Seeded procedural moth generation on Canvas 2D with five body-plan families and per-genus, per-species parameters - Parametric wing outlines (quadratic margins with scallops, angular points, tails and hooked apices) and a wing-space (u,v) coordinate system so bands, veins, mottling and fringes follow the wing's own curvature - Layered wing painting: radial base gradient, median shading, scale-stroke mottling, wavy and dentate transverse bands with pale companions, kidney marks, discal dots and concentric eyespots with highlights, radiating veins, hair fringe - One side drawn and mirrored with a reseeded generator for exact bilateral symmetry, then asymmetric wear cut in with destination-out compositing and truncated antennae - Furry thorax and segmented abdomen built from batched radial strokes; pectinate or thread-like antennae along a Bézier - Shadows baked per specimen and scaled with wingspan; CSS-drawn steel pin heads with specular dots - Resolution-independent 3× re-render with extra detail, cached offscreen and panned beneath a conic-gradient brass rim with masked ring, glass highlights and a turned handle - Walnut grain, paper fibre and page grain from inline SVG turbulence; procedurally scattered foxing as stacked radial gradients; mitred frame corners via clip-path - Glass reflection streaks that drift with the pointer - Web Animations choreography: drawer slide with settling overshoot, 35ms staggered setting-in, two-stage card-turn flip with perspective - Index-card catalogue with ruled lines, red header rule, punched hole and typewriter text reveal - Steering-noise flight simulation with flapping wing foreshortening, heading-aligned body and an altitude shadow - Typographic system of Didot/Bodoni numerals, Baskerville italics, letterspaced small caps, Georgia italic handwriting with per-word ink opacity, and Courier typing

notes.zh: 作者自述：The viewer stands inside the lift car of the Hotel Meridian, a sixty-storey Art Deco hotel of 1931, and scrolling is riding. The screen is fixed: two brushed-brass doors engraved with chevrons and a rising sunburst, a semicircular brass floor indicator above them, verdigris wall panels either side, a strip of veined black marble underfoot. As the page scrolls the indicator hand springs from floor to floor, shaft lines streak through the gap between the doors, and at ten floors the car stops, sways, and the doors slide apart on a small flat Deco scene with one looping motion each: a revolving door, a spinning globe, waltzing silhouettes under a mirror ball, a swinging bulb on bare brick, parrots on perches, dripping lost umbrellas, a cake being iced at 3 a.m., a lone swimmer under the moon, a tram crossing below a telescope, and finally the roof with the hotel's neon sign seen backwards against the dawn. Each scene is captioned in the dry, discreet voice of the attendant, Mr. Abernathy. The mood is luxurious, nocturnal and slightly haunted; the whole page is lit by brass against lacquer black.

tags: - Fixed-viewport CSS grid "car" with a tall invisible scroll track; scroll position is mapped through a timeline of title, stop and travel segments to floor number and door openness - Floor indicator built procedurally in inline SVG (60 ticks, 59 lamps, engraved numerals, ivory dial, brass gradients) with a hand driven by a damped-spring simulation and a blurred lamp glow that follows the current floor - Door engraving (chevrons, title band, sunburst, ziggurat steps) generated as SVG line work at the exact pixel size of each panel, drawn twice for an incised highlight-and-shadow look; brushed metal from layered repeating gradients - Doors moved by transforms bound to a single CSS custom property, which also drives vignette scale, caption reveal and the light spilling into the car - Ten hand-drawn flat SVG vignettes in the five-colour palette, each with CSS keyframe loops (scaleX "revolving" wings, clipped scrolling continents, dash-array mirror-ball dots, pendulum bulb, stroke-dashoffset icing, wave translation, mirrored neon text with blur glow, rotating searchlight beams) - Canvas streak lines in the door gap, positioned in "shaft space" so their speed and motion blur follow the car's velocity - Marble floor veining and film grain from feTurbulence filters; stepped Deco wall panels via clip-path and layered box-shadows - Tall, thin Deco numerals made by vertically scaling a light geometric sans; widely tracked gold capitals; ivory serif italic captions - Web Audio synthesis (off by default): filtered oscillator hum tied to speed, brown-noise door rumble tied to door velocity, tick per floor, three-partial arrival bell - Entrance sequence in which the car lights flicker on and the hand settles to L; reduced-motion mode cross-fades the doors and removes streaks, sway, spring and loops

title.zh: Side A — A Turntable in CSS
title.en: Side A — A Turntable in CSS

notes.zh: 作者自述：A catalogue-style spread for an invented 1974 turntable, the Marlowe PL·7, playing an invented jazz LP, "Slow Weather" by the Marguerite Okonkwo Quintet. A walnut plinth with a cream deck plate sits tilted in real perspective under a translucent sage dust cover, in front of a burnt-orange supergraphic sun and sage shelf stripes; a fat italic "Side A" headline, a sleeve note, a leaning record sleeve and a track list sit to the left, and a brushed-aluminium amplifier with two VU meters and a pair of walnut speakers complete the system. The page looks like a still illustration until the viewer presses START: the lamp and strobe light up, the record gathers speed, the arm rises, crosses to the lead-in groove, settles, and begins a four-minute walk toward the label while the meters dance, the speakers breathe arcs and slanted window light slowly warms the page. Everything is drawn from HTML elements and gradients and everything moves without a line of script.

tags: - 3-D scene with perspective and preserve-3d: tilted deck plane, plinth front face, feet, ground shadow, and a four-face hinged dust cover that rotates about its back edge - Walnut veneer from stacked repeating-linear and repeating elliptical radial gradients at slightly different angles, plus fine pore noise - Brushed aluminium from conic gradients over fine repeating gradients (platter, pivot, knobs, amplifier face, button cap) - Vinyl from repeating-radial-gradient grooves, radial track-gap bands, a rotating conic glint masked to the groove area and a separate fixed sheen - Strobe rim: two repeating-conic-gradient dot rows cut to rings with radial masks, one standing still and one drifting according to speed - Record label text set around the rim letter by letter with per-letter rotation - Jump-free spin-up and run-down: a paused/running steady rotation nested inside a wrapper whose transition is a decelerating counter-turn of exactly one revolution; a second nested rotor adds the difference between 33⅓ and 45 - Tonearm choreography entirely from transitions: two nested rotors (swing, then four-minute tracking), with lift expressed through registered custom properties (@property) that drive scale and a drop-shadow offset - "Freeze in place" cue pause using a new transition target with an effectively endless delay - VU needles driven by an animated registered number multiplied by signal gates, so they rise after the stylus lands and fall when it lifts - Speaker arcs from single-sided circular borders scaled and faded on staggered loops - Supergraphic background: corner radial-gradient sun with rings, stripe set built from nested bordered boxes sharing a concentric rounded corner - Record sleeve artwork from circles and pill shapes, with ring wear and a sliding inner sleeve - Stacked hard offset text-shadows on the display type; paper tooth overlay from repeating radial gradients - Whole hi-fi sized in em from one viewport-derived unit, with two layouts and a reduced-motion variant

notes.zh: 作者自述：A parish census drawn as a single sheet of cream paper: on the left, a small masthead and seven questions set as large serif sentences; on the right, one enormous numeral, a phrase that completes it, and three hundred coloured dots that are, each of them, somebody. The dots rain in and settle into a packed cluster of households; ask another question and every family lifts off together, arcs across the page and springs into place as a population pyramid, nineteen clusters of occupation, a hand-ruled map of six streets under a hill, a beeswarm of arrival years, a choir on its risers above a grey audience, or a ring of friendships. The headline counts to its new value, the rules and labels draw themselves in, and a sentence written from the data sits underneath, dry and affectionate. Hovering any dot produces a little card with a name, an age and a one-line life; pinning it lets you follow one person through every statistic they belong to.

tags: - Single 2D canvas rendering 300 dots with per-dot position, radius, colour and outline interpolation, DPR-aware (capped at 2), drawn only when something changes - Transitions along individual quadratic Bezier paths driven by an analytic under-damped spring (about 4% overshoot), with delays ordered household by household according to destination - Rain-in entrance with gravity easing and a small bounce; cross-fade variant for reduced motion - Seeded generator (mulberry32) building households, ages, sexes, names, streets, occupations, arrival years, choir voices and best-friend links with exact quotas - Packed-circle cluster from a small collision/cohesion relaxation that keeps households adjacent; phyllotaxis clumps for occupations and households - Dot-stacked population pyramid, flow-packed occupation clusters sized to fit, beeswarm with collision search and auto-fitted radius, pew grid with aisle, staggered double ring with curved chords - Schematic map from Catmull-Rom curves with a slight hand wobble: streets, river, railway with sleepers, hill contours, church, station, mill wheel and geese, all drawn in thin lines - Progressive "draw-in" of every rule, axis, leader line, link and label via partial polyline stroking and staggered fades - Text set along a circular arc for street names on the friendship ring; haloed labels on the map - Spatial hash grid for hit-testing; highlight layer with rings, household lines and a dashed or solid coral friend curve - Hand-drawn SVG underlines revealed with clip-path, hand-ruled search line, drawn die and masthead vignette, SVG turbulence paper grain - Count-up tabular numerals, cross-faded headline, legend and generated insight sentence

notes.zh: 作者自述：A quiet potter's studio on a single screen: linen wall with a patch of window light, a bench with a dusty blue water bucket and two spare balls of clay, and in the middle a charcoal splash pan with 900 g of wet terracotta turning on the wheel head. The page opens with the lump wobbling into centre and a pair of ghost fingers opening it and making one pull, so the clay rises in the first seconds; then the viewer takes over and the wall follows their fingers, getting taller as it is collared, squatter as it is bellied, thinner as it is pulled, and folding into a heap if it is rushed. Around the wheel the type is set like a craft catalogue: small-caps labels, potter's notes in tiny italic numerals, a hand-drawn tool rack and one large italic line, "Centre. Open. Pull. Breathe.", whose words light in turn. Wiring the pot off begins the second act: it is lifted on tongs, dipped into a bucket of glaze, watched through a glowing kiln peephole while the cones bend and the counter climbs to 1,240 °C, and comes out glossy to slide onto a wooden shelf that fills up over the session.

tags: - Canvas 2D lathe solid: an 80-sample radius profile drawn as stacked elliptical strips, each with its own nine-stop gradient computed from a Lambert term, a specular term, edge darkening and a reflected rim light, including the slope of the wall - Throwing rings as dashed elliptical arcs whose dash offset scrolls with the wheel angle, plus drifting wet specular streaks and slip drips sliding down the wall - Hollow interior with lit far wall, visible floor ellipse and a rim that rocks when it is uneven; off-centre wobble as a height-weighted sinusoidal offset - Soft-shaded finger sprites rendered once off-screen, faded along their length and clipped so the inside finger disappears behind the front wall - Material system for wet clay, leather-hard clay, chalky raw glaze, bisque and five fired glazes: pooled colour in the rings, sharp vertical highlights, seeded iron speckle, ash runs with beads, a wavering glaze line and bare foot ring made with a clip path - Kiln peephole: procedural brick wall, additive bloom, black-body colour ramp driven by temperature, flicker, pot silhouette and three pyrometric cones bent as curved tapered polygons - Glaze bucket with liquid surface clipping, ripples and falling drops; FLIP-style flight of the finished pot from the stage to its place on the shelf - Hand-drawn SVG tools, a pedal-shaped range thumb, CSS wood plank with grain, paper grain overlay generated in code - Optional Web Audio: filtered oscillators for the wheel hum, band-passed noise for wet friction, low roar in the kiln and small pings as the glaze cools

notes.zh: 作者自述：A cold room at 2 a.m., seen as one full-bleed window: four panes in a dark wooden frame, a sodium-lit street dissolved into heptagonal bokeh behind them, and frost drawing itself across the glass in real time. The first ferns shoot out of the lower-left corner, then everything slows to a patient creep: curved plumes with herringbone side branches at sixty degrees, six-armed frost flowers, lines of ice running along invisible scratches, all stopping where they meet older ice so the pane fills over about two minutes yet keeps clear islands. Where the ice is dense the street behind turns pale and diffuse, and crystals glint when a lamp or a passing car's headlights slide behind them. Hold a finger to the glass and a haze of breath blooms, the frost melts outward into beads, a few drops run down leaving clear tracks, and when you let go the patch quietly freezes over again with ferns that were never there before. The only words are "breathe here", fingertip-written in old condensation and already half frozen, a thermometer on the frame, and a tiny caption on the sill.

tags: - Canvas 2D growth simulation: hundreds of advancing tips with curvature, alternating side branches at plus and minus 60 degrees, promoted leader branches, directly drawn barbs, and six-armed nucleation stars - Occupancy grid collision so ferns stop at existing ice and at the frame, with noisy elliptical exclusion zones that keep clear islands - Incremental drawing: only new segments are stroked each frame into an offscreen frost canvas, with later passes thickening older stems - Low-resolution density mask used to composite a blurred, lightened copy of the street through the frost (refraction and glow) - Procedural out-of-focus street: feathered seven-bladed bokeh sprites with additive blending, pulsing lamps, a cycling traffic light, passing headlights, drifting snow, and a roofline and branches blurred by repeated downsampling - Sparkle system: sampled crystal points flare as four-point glints only when a light disc lies behind them - Breath: radial fog patches tinted by the blurred street and pitted with a droplet pattern, destination-out melting of frost and mask, condensation beads with highlights, stick-slip runner drops carving trails, beads that freeze in place - Regrowth: melted zones remember their rim and reseed fast inward-growing ferns after a delay - Hand-built single-stroke lettering for "breathe here", punched out of a condensation haze with a refrozen ridge and small crystals across it - Canvas-drawn wood frame, muntin cross and sill with grain, bevel highlight and sodium light on the ledges; inline SVG thermometer and radiator icon - Web Audio: filtered brown-noise wind with slow modulation, randomised metallic radiator ticks, band-passed breath - Entrance time-warp (fast then slowing), devicePixelRatio capped at 2, capped tip counts, loop paused when the tab is hidden, pre-grown static variant for reduced motion

notes.zh: 作者自述：A fine-press book of five pages on warm paper, in blue-black ink with one red mark per page. The cover sets "Five" in italic over an enormous "Calligrams." and types its subtitle onto a pale wave. Each page then performs its poem: Rain falls in slanted columns of words that splash letter by letter at the ground and part around one red, dry "umbrella"; River carries a long sentence down a meander, letters springing at the source, swelling where two small tributary sentences run into it; Heron stands as a bird made of type and, when ready, lunges its neck of words at the water as "not yet" becomes "now"; Stair lets the reader's scroll bounce a red full stop down seventeen word-steps to the floor; Breath opens and closes a ring of words at four seconds in and six out. Any poem can be un-shaped into plain stanzas and shaped again, so the reader can watch form become, and stop being, meaning.

tags: - Real, selectable SVG text on per-line paths (textPath), rebuilt in pixel units for the actual stage size so type stays between 13 and about 40px on every screen - Flow by re-sampling each clause's sub-path along an arclength table of the meander every frame, with negative startOffset at the source and natural glyph clipping at the mouth and confluences - Type that swells at confluences through a size function integrated along the river, so each clause exactly fills its widening stretch - Path morphing: Catmull-Rom paths interpolated point by point (polar interpolation about the shoulder for the heron's strike; staggered shaped-to-straight morph for "read plainly") - Letter-by-letter write-in using paired visible/transparent tspans, so layout never shifts while the text appears along its path - A displacement field that parts falling columns and streaks around the umbrella; ballistic letter splashes and expanding ripple arcs at the ground line - Dynamic letterspacing for the breathing circle, the heron's elastic neck and its spaced-letter legs - Scroll-linked sticky page with parabolic hops, squash-and-stretch, dipping treads and dash-revealed ghost arcs - Ghost paths in pale grey-blue hairlines: water strands, canopy, stair profile, breathing limits, a ten-second dial - Paper grain from an inline feTurbulence filter; hairline rules, tracked small caps, dotted leaders - Responsive recomputation of every geometry (portrait meander, switchback staircase) and a composed still frame for reduced motion

title.zh: Conservas Maré Alta — Tinned Fish Since 1923
title.en: Conservas Maré Alta — Tinned Fish Since 1923

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sunny, proud landing page for the invented cannery Conservas Maré Alta of Porto Salgado, drawn entirely as mid-century tinned-fish packaging: flat inks in cream, tomato red, sea teal, sun yellow and navy, halftone-dot shadows, off-register outlines, arched banners and numerals in ovals. A red hero patterned with tiny fish carries the headline "The sea, kept." beside an oversized, tilted tin whose wrapper comes alive (sunrays turning, a sardine leaping with a splash beside a striped lighthouse). The centrepiece is "A Nossa Lata": a lithographed tin whose lid curls around its key as you scroll, drag or press Abrir, uncovering six scaled, gleaming sardines laid head-to-tail in shimmering golden oil with a bay leaf and a slice of chili. Below sit a yellow shelf of six differently designed tins that turn over to show ingredients, a one-line serving suggestion and an escudo price sticker; a teal strip of six perforated stamps telling the process; a typed letter from fourth-generation owner Inês Carvalhal with a hand-drawn signature; and a footer shaped like the embossed bottom of a tin, with stockists, factory visits and a newsletter that answers with a rubber stamp.

tags: - Inline SVG illustration throughout: hero wrapper, six distinct tin labels, six process stamps, price stickers, letterhead mark and signature, all in the five brief colours plus tinplate tints - Text on curved banners with SVG textPath, fitted with textLength so labels hold their shape in any condensed fallback font - Print texture: halftone-dot shadows from repeating radial gradients and SVG patterns, 1-2px off-register duplicate outlines and lettering, a fine turbulence paper grain over the whole page - The opening tin: a clip-path lid that retreats under a gradient-shaded roll whose radius grows as it winds, travelling seam lines and a foreshortened key loop to suggest rotation, a jagged torn edge revealed by a second clip, cast and lift shadows that follow the roll - Sardines built from a reusable symbol with a silver gradient sheen, an arc scale pattern, gill plates and lateral dots; oil shimmer from animated dashed highlights and a sweeping glint - An oil drop that runs down the roll, falls and leaves a small stain on the paper - Spring-eased "label being pasted" entrances (rotation settling to square) driven by IntersectionObserver, with a linear() spring curve - Scrolling wave borders made from repeating SVG tiles; slowly rotating sunrays; a one-time leap and splash on load - 3D rotateY tin flips with preserved backfaces; pointer-proximity bobbing along the shelf - Perforated stamp edges from a radial-gradient hole grid; embossed batch code from layered text shadows; rubber stamp roughened with turbulence and displacement filters - A custom fish-fork cursor on fine pointers - Reduced-motion variant: no rotation, bobbing or scrolling waves, and the lid simply fades away

notes.zh: 作者自述：A wall of Victorian instruments mounted on grained mahogany: a great aneroid barometer at the centre, ringed by an anemometer, a 32-point wind rose, a psychrometer, a rain gauge, a clockwork barograph in a glazed case, a sunshine recorder and a cluster of small dials for tide, sea and visibility, all under a brass plaque. Nothing is a number in a box; every value is a needle, a mercury column, a water level or an ink line. A week of invented weather runs on a fast clock, and a deep Atlantic low arrives a few seconds after the page opens: the barometer needle sinks heavily into the red sector, the vane backs and twitches, the anemometer surges with each gust, rain streaks cross the window reflected in every glass, the light dims, and a red storm cone climbs the signal mast while the observer's log writes its warning in a slanting hand. Then the front goes through, the vane flies round to the north-west, and the glass leaps. The experience is meant to be calm and exact, like standing in a quiet room while the weather happens outside.

tags: - Every instrument built procedurally as inline SVG: bezels, screws, tick rings, rotated numerals and arc-set lettering generated from scale functions - Brass rendered with layered multi-stop linear gradients (highlight, body, shadow) in opposed directions for a bevelled look; enamel faces with radial gradients - Damped-spring simulation per needle with individual stiffness and damping, gust noise built from summed sines, stiction on the barometer and micro-tremble - Deterministic weather model: skewed Gaussian depression, gradient-driven wind, backing and veering direction, frontal rain band, humidity, visibility, wave height and tide, precomputed over a looping 168-hour week - Barograph drum drawn in cylindrical projection: time lines, day labels and the violet trace are remapped through a sine each frame so the paper visibly turns; aneroid stack and pen arm are linked to the pressure - Glass layer on each dial with a four-pane window reflection whose angle and strength follow the cloud cover, and an animated SVG pattern of rain streaks clipped to that reflection - Wood grain from an feTurbulence filter with stretched frequency, plank seams and vignette; drifting cloud shadow and a warm lamp glow at night - Storm cone hoisted with a spring-eased transform, flipping orientation with the wind; pennant flutter rate tied to wind speed - Sunshine card scorched segment by segment with width and darkness set by the simulated sun - Enlarging transition that moves the live instrument itself into a detail view, with a history chart whose ink line draws itself - Log entries revealed with a pen-speed clip-path wipe on ruled paper; typeset synopsis with a drop capital

notes.zh: 作者自述：A hushed stone nave seen from the floor: a wall of ashlar blocks, a pointed arch with carved mouldings, two dark columns, and high in the wall a rose window whose several hundred pieces of ruby, cobalt, gold, emerald, amethyst and pale glass are generated afresh by gothic rules of symmetry, nested rings, lancets, foils and roundels. The viewer holds the sun. As it moves, a hotspot of brilliance travels across the glass, bright pieces bloom over their leads, and the whole window is thrown down as a long, soft, skewed pool of colour across the flagstones, with tinted dust sparkling in the shaft between. Each new commission is drawn in lead from the centre outward and then glazed ring by ring, every piece flaring as it is set, while a carved inscription records its order and opus number.
