tags: - Full-bleed Canvas 2D scene composited from pre-rendered layers (wall, floor joints, columns, glass, leads, stone tracery) - Seeded procedural window generator: polar lancets with pointed or round heads, cusped foils traced as unions of circles, circle-packed roundels and eyelets, quarry and diamond borders - Rule-based colour assignment (dominant pair alternating by ring and position, gold borders and centres, foliage bands) with per-piece hue jitter - Per-piece glass rendering: off-centre radial gradient, blown-glass streaks, seed bubbles, dark matting near the lead, painted grisaille strokes - Stone tracery with per-edge directional bevel shading and concentric carved mouldings, cut out with destination-out - Per-frame lighting with multiply, saturation and color-dodge blend passes plus a downsampled additive halation pass - Row-by-row perspective projection of the lit window onto the floor with shear, stretch, blur and additive blending; flagstone joints redrawn over the light - Dust motes placed in the three-dimensional light shaft, coloured by sampling the glass they pass beneath, with twinkling star glints - Animated lead strokes using dash offsets, staggered glazing with additive setting flares, cross-fade from the previous window - Four eased times of day (dawn, noon, dusk, moonlit night) retinting glass, masonry and projection - Inscription and floor-slab hint set in tracked serif capitals with carved text shadows and CSS perspective

notes.zh: 作者自述：A bright, paper-coloured tangram table in the manner of a mid-century picture book. The title is drawn letter by letter in chunky geometric strokes so that every counter and arch can hold a small coloured triangle. Seven flat-coloured wooden pieces begin as the classic square, burst apart into a loose scatter, and a pale dotted silhouette draws itself onto the work mat. The viewer drags, turns and flips the pieces until the shape is covered; the seams then glow, the silhouette fades, and the finished figure wakes up while still visibly made of its seven pieces: a swan glides over ripples, a cat blinks and swishes its tail, a rabbit hops, a fish wags through bubbles, a dancer sways, a boat rocks on waves, a house puffs smoke, a bird flaps. A lettered caption reports the time, and a vermilion stamp is pressed into a row of eight.

tags: - Inline SVG stage with exact tangram geometry on square and diagonal unit lattices; every silhouette is a true union of the seven pieces - Silhouette outline computed in the page by splitting and cancelling shared edges, drawn as a dotted line revealed through an animated stroke mask - Shape-based solution test by sampling points of the silhouette against the pieces' polygons, so interchangeable pieces and alternative solutions count - Hand-rolled spring physics for position, rotation, lift, flip and snap squash, with staggered toss choreography - Creature animation by composing body and limb transforms over the pieces the viewer actually placed, plus small drawn extras (eyes, ripples, bubbles, waves, smoke, notes) - Title lettering constructed from SVG strokes with triangles popping into the counters - Procedural paper grain tile drawn once to canvas, wood-grain lines clipped to each piece, blurred short shadows that deepen on lift - Print-style flat controls with hard offset shadows, dotted rules, stamp marks and tabular numerals - Optional synthesised sound: wooden clicks and a pentatonic flourish

notes.zh: 作者自述：A Halden Portable, Model 5, sits on a lamp-lit wooden desk in 1958. A sheet of warm paper rises out of its black rubber platen and fills the upper part of the view; below it are the grey-green enamel deck with its fan of steel type bars, two ribbon spools, a nickel nameplate, a strike counter, and a bank of round glass-topped keys. The machine types its own first line with a human rhythm, returns the carriage, and then waits with a pulsing red caret at the printing point. From there every key the viewer presses is a physical event: the key sinks, a type bar leaps from the basket, the ribbon jumps, the paper shudders, an imperfect inked letter lands and settles, and the whole carriage steps one space to the left. Nothing can be erased, only struck over. Finished sheets are pulled out and drift onto a fanned pile that can be read again.

tags: - Per-glyph ink synthesis on a 2D canvas: each character is drawn to an offscreen stamp with a fill plus a heavier outline, then cut by a randomly offset alpha mask combining low-frequency blotch noise, a diagonal ribbon-weave pattern and dropout specks, and multiplied onto the sheet so overstrikes darken - Persistent per-slug misalignment (every character has its own fixed offset and tilt; the e always sits a hair high) plus per-strike jitter, speed-dependent ink density, occasional clogged e and a counters, ghost double impressions, and black bleed at the top of red letters - Procedural paper: flecks and curved fibres drawn into each sheet, with the unfed part of the sheet standing behind the platen and a wrap shadow where the paper curls around the roller - Type basket generated as SVG: 42 type bars on a foreshortened elliptical fan, each mapped to one key; a struck bar is redrawn per frame along a quadratic arc to the printing point with a thickening that fakes depth, a motion smear, and a cubic snap-back - Carriage built from layered CSS gradients (rubber platen, knurled knobs, chrome paper bail with engraved scale, tab-stop marks, rubber rollers) moved by transform transitions with overshooting cubic-bezier steps and a long eased return - Round keys made from a conic-gradient nickel rim on the border box, a dark legend disc on the padding box and a glass highlight overlay, with spring-curved press and release - Wet-ink settle: a blurred duplicate of each letter fades and contracts over the fresh impression - Sheet ejection choreographed with the Web Animations API: an accelerating pull out of the platen, then a measured flight with rotation and a soft landing on the pile - Synthesised sound with the Web Audio API: noise bursts through resonant band-pass filters pitched per key, a low thump for the space bar, a three-partial sine bell, a ratcheting zip for the return, a dull thud for the jammed margin, a rising tear for the pulled sheet - Lamp-light atmosphere: a radial pool of warm light over a wood-grain desk, a deep brown vignette, tiled film grain, and an enamel lamp shade with a brass rim in the corner - Mechanical details: rolling five-digit strike counter, spools that advance with every strike, a bell dome that rings visibly, a ribbon vibrator that lifts higher for red than for black

notes.zh: 作者自述：A flat, saturated tangerine living-room wall carries a supergraphic of seven concentric stripes that sweeps in from the left edge and bends down around a single rocket-shaped lava lamp standing on the edge of a teak sideboard. The lamp's spun-aluminium cap and hourglass base frame a tapered glass vessel in which glossy magenta wax lifts off a settled mound, stretches, necks to a thread, pinches in two, cools at the top and sinks again, all in amber liquid with drifting sparkle, a specular streak and a small window reflected on the glass. Fat cream Cooper-style lettering with a stepped aubergine drop-shade sits low on the wall beside it, over a quiet lowercase caption that says "wait for it." until a blob lets go. The page opens cold: the stripes draw themselves, the title springs up, the bulb flickers on, its glow spreads up the wall and the first big blob leaves the mound. The mood is warm, drowsy and unapologetically 1971.

tags: - Hand-written WebGL fragment shader summing a finite-support metaball field (12 simulated blobs, 3 neck threads, 1 mound) with a smooth antialiased threshold - Pseudo-normals from the analytic field gradient for wrap diffuse, twin-lobe specular, rim transmission, under-lighting from the bulb and temperature-driven wax colour - Glass rendered in the shader: outline mask, cylindrical-lens compression toward the edges, edge darkening, vertical specular streaks, curved four-pane window reflection, suspended twinkling sparkle - JavaScript thermal simulation: per-blob temperature, buoyancy, viscous drag, soft collisions, velocity sharing, bonded pairs that break and neck, anisotropic velocity stretch - Lamp metalwork from CSS conic gradients converging on each cone's apex, with fine spin lines and aubergine-toned shadows - SVG supergraphic stripes drawn in with stroke-dash animation and recoloured by staggered overlay sweeps; wall recoloured by an expanding clip-path circle from the lamp - SVG title lettering fattened and softened with round-joined strokes and a stacked drop-shade, fitted to its ink bounds at load - Wall and tabletop glow that pulses with wax passing the bulb; feTurbulence paper grain and anisotropic teak grain - Enamel control plate in CSS: knurled rotary dimmer, pilot jewel, three domed colour chips - Fallback without WebGL: blurred circles under an SVG contrast (gooey) filter animated by keyframes inside the clipped glass

notes.zh: 作者自述：A white-cube gallery rendered as a long page: an entrance wall with the museum's name in enormous tight black grotesque under a single blue waveform that dies away into a flat line, then nine exhibit rows, each with a huge outlined catalogue number, a single-weight line drawing standing on a plinth, and a wall label written in a dry curatorial voice. The front face of every plinth is an instrument panel: a round blue button, an oscilloscope and a small spectrogram that show the sound actually being made at that moment. Nothing is recorded; a rotary dial, a modem handshake, a typewriter, a television, a camera, a floppy drive, a cassette, a slide projector and the time pips are all built from oscillators, filtered noise and envelopes, and each drawing performs one exact mechanical movement in step with its sound. The modem is the centrepiece: its plinth panel widens across the whole row and a large spectrogram writes itself out while brackets caption the conversation between the two machines. A mechanical tally counts what has been heard, and the exit wall keeps its last label in storage until all nine have played.

tags: - Inline SVG line drawings with one non-scaling stroke weight, blue-only accents, and parts animated by transforms (rotating dial wheel, sliding carriage, iris, head carriage, reels, clock hands) - Web Audio synthesis patches per exhibit: oscillators, band-passed noise bursts, pitch-dropping thumps, amplitude modulation, frequency-shift keying, a computed tune buffer with playback-rate automation for tape wow and fast-forward - Live oscilloscope on canvas from an AnalyserNode with zero-crossing trigger and automatic gain, devicePixelRatio-aware - Scrolling canvas spectrograms per exhibit with a frequency range chosen for each sound - Full-row modem spectrogram written to an offscreen buffer and blitted with grid lines, playhead, time and frequency axes, and timed caption brackets revealed with clip-path - Idle and reduced-motion envelope plots drawn from each patch's timing data - Outlined display numerals using text stroke with paint-order, and very large negative-tracked grotesque headlines sized in viewport units - Entrance waveform simulated as a damped string (1D wave equation) that reacts to pointer movement - Television static drawn into a low-resolution pixelated canvas, and a CSS keyframed collapse of the picture into a line and then a dot - Mechanical tally drums with overshoot easing, progress ring around each play button, level meter in the master control - Rules and label text that draw in from the left via IntersectionObserver, with custom cubic-bezier easing throughout

notes.zh: 作者自述：A fixed sky above a stubble field outside the invented village of Ellery, where a small crowd, two tripods, a dog and a single ash tree wait for a total eclipse. Scrolling is time: the Moon bites into a pale warm Sun, the blue sky thins to steel and then to twilight indigo, the field drains to silver, shadows harden, and an inset shows the ground under the tree covered in crescent suns. In the last minute shadow bands ripple over the field, the umbra rises from the west, the crescent breaks into Baily's beads along a jagged lunar limb and collapses into a diamond ring with bloom and diffraction spikes. Then the page goes dark: a delicate, asymmetric, shimmering corona unfurls around a black Moon, pink prominences cling to the limb, Venus and stars appear, the horizon glows orange all the way round, rooks fly to roost, the dog howls, and the word TOTALITY breathes across the sky above the quiet line "Two minutes, eleven seconds." Scrolling on plays it all in reverse on the opposite limb until daylight, colour and an ordinary afternoon return and people pack up. A clock, a contact timeline, a thermometer that falls six degrees and a needle light meter keep the facts while sparse second-person annotations keep the feeling.

tags: - One fixed full-viewport 2D canvas (DPR capped at 2) redrawn from a single eased scroll-progress value; everything is reversible - Real eclipse geometry: circle-intersection area drives the light level, sky keyframes, land colour, shadow sharpness and readouts - Sky built from four interpolated six-stop gradients (day blue, steel, indigo, totality with a sunset-orange horizon band) - Procedural corona: polar texture of noise-modulated rays, tapering equatorial streamers and fanning polar plumes, tone-mapped and pre-rendered to two offscreen buffers that are cross-faded, slightly counter-rotated and radially masked to unfurl - Fixed jagged lunar limb profile (720 samples) used both to draw the Moon and to compute which valleys still pass sunlight, producing Baily's beads and the final diamond - Diamond ring with additive bloom sprite, eight tapered diffraction spikes, soft halo ring and lens ghosts along the optical axis - Pink prominences and chromosphere arc drawn on the Sun's limb and uncovered asymmetrically by the Moon's motion - Landscape of layered hills, village with spire, furrowed field, ash tree and a crowd of silhouettes whose colours desaturate toward silver and fall to black against the horizon glow - Radial-gradient shadows whose penumbra narrows as the Sun becomes a sliver; wavy moving shadow bands clipped to the field; umbra as a growing dark radial wall from the west - "Look down" inset: 280 pinhole images stamped from a live crescent sprite matching the current phase, inverted as a pinhole would - Twinkling stars, labelled planets, a flock of flapping birds crossing the orange band, a howling dog with drifting letters - DOM typography over the canvas: Georgia annotations with small-caps time stamps, thin wide-tracked sans for TOTALITY with per-letter breathing spacing, ink colour that switches with sky and field luminance - SVG needle light meter, thermometer readout, vertical contact timeline with live clock; film grain overlay - Reduced-motion mode: scroll progress quantised into discrete stages, no shimmer, flicker, grain jitter or shadow bands

title.zh: Kestrel Frameworks — Bicycles Drawn to Measure
title.en: Kestrel Frameworks — Bicycles Drawn to Measure

notes.zh: 作者自述：The page is four folded cyanotype sheets from the drawing office of a one-woman frame shop in an invented Calder-valley town. Sheet 1 opens by drafting a fully dimensioned side elevation of a lugged steel touring frame, fork, wheels and a dotted rider under a headline lettered across the whole width of the sheet, with a schedule of dimensions and a pencilled margin note from the builder. Sheet 2 hands the viewer four scale rules; moving any of them recalculates a real frame geometry and the drawing redraws itself tube by tube, numbers rolling and flashing marking-out yellow, construction arcs swinging through the tube ends, the rider leaning further forward or sitting up, the wheels shrinking to 650B for short legs, while every change is logged as a lettered revision that also updates the drawing number in each title block. Sheet 3 shows three circular detail views of the joinery with numbered balloons and the builder's reasons in her own hand. Sheet 4 sets out fourteen weeks of work as a hatched bar chart, plain prices, an apologetic waiting list, and a request form that carries the viewer's figures and ends with a yellow RECEIVED stamp slammed onto the title block. Everything is line work in four colours on blotchy blue paper with fold creases, masked borders and zone marks.

tags: - Parametric bicycle geometry solver (seat tube, effective top tube, stack, reach, head tube, fork, wheelbase, trail, standover) driving two live inline-SVG drawings from one shared state - Tubes drawn as double strokes (white outer, field-blue inner) so joints occlude correctly and each tube can be drafted with stroke-dashoffset - Staged draft-in choreography with per-element delays and a custom cubic-bezier: centre lines, tubes, compass-swept wheels, components, rider, dimensions - Exponential-chase interpolation of rider parameters each frame, so every line, arrowhead, angle arc and numeral moves and rolls continuously - Two-link inverse kinematics for the dotted rider's legs, torso and arms - Aligned, rotated dimension lines with computed arrowheads, extension lines, angle arcs and halo-knocked-out mono numerals - Yellow construction arcs swept through tube ends with the Web Animations API when a length or angle changes - Line weights, dash patterns and lettering sized through CSS custom properties recomputed from the drawing's on-screen width - Cyanotype texture from four layered SVG feTurbulence filters (dark blotching, pale bloom, paper fibre, fine grain) on a fixed overlay - CSS fold creases, lighter masked border, zone letters and numbers, and a CSS-grid title block on every sheet - Headline set as SVG text with textLength so it spans the sheet exactly, stroked in on load - Custom scale-rule sliders built from generated tick marks with a yellow index, ARIA slider semantics and pointer capture - Hand-plotted circular detail drawings (head lug with feather window, fillet-brazed bottom bracket, dropout) with clip paths, hidden-line and centre-line styles, and stroke-drawn reveal on scroll - CSS-grid Gantt chart with hatched bars growing from the left on entry - Hovering kestrel logo with rapid alternating wing rotation triggered only when the page is idle - Rubber-stamp animation with an overshoot easing for the RECEIVED mark

notes.zh: 作者自述：A museum-cabinet instrument on sunlit plaster: a dark walnut frame carries a row of brass bobs on fine strings, their lengths cut so that each makes one more swing per minute than its neighbour. A hinged release bar holds them to one side, lifts, and the row leaves in unison, then slides into a travelling wave, tangles, sorts itself into four, three and two interleaved groups, and at exactly sixty seconds sweeps back into one line while a brass ring spreads from the frame and the dial glows. Beneath the frame the same row is seen from above as a single undulating line with a fading wake; at the side a brass-bezelled sixty-second dial names the pattern of the moment and states the arithmetic behind it; along the bottom a brass rule lets the viewer slide to any instant. Everything is computed from the closed-form angle, so any moment can be visited exactly and the minute repeats forever without drift.

tags: - Canvas 2D front view in oblique projection with per-frame depth sorting, so bobs pass in front of and behind one another and the frame posts - Pendulum lengths computed from g(T/2π)² and drawn true to scale, with an engraved centimetre scale on the post - Pre-rendered brass sphere sprite: offset radial gradient, window-pane specular, cool bounce light from the wall, dark rim - Soft slate wall shadows for bobs, strings, frame and bar, with parallax and blur that grow as a bob nears the viewer - Analytic motion blur: ghost exposures sampled at earlier instants of the exact solution rather than from a frame buffer - Top view with a Catmull-Rom spline through the bobs and a fading history of fifteen earlier curves, also sampled analytically - SVG dial generated in code: brass bezel gradient, sixty engraved ticks, diamond marks and tiny dot diagrams for the famous moments, sweeping hand; a slim arc version for phones - Brass rule scrubber with engraved ticks, numerals and a glass slide-rule rider; brass plaque title with chamfered corners and rivets - Plaster wall built from an SVG turbulence grain, a slow-drifting skewed window-light pattern and a slate vignette - Expanding thin brass rings and a dial flash choreographed to the sixty-second return - Web Audio struck-bar voices (sine plus inharmonic partial, exponential decay, stereo pan by position) on a two-octave pentatonic scale

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sunlit blush tabletop with a cream toy-like instant camera called the dawdle, its teal neck strap looped off to the side, a small box of film, and eight dashed outlines waiting for pictures. Pressing the red shutter fires a white flash, the iris blinks, the camera kicks, and a square print is pushed out of the slot in motor steps, drops free and glides to its numbered place at a slight tilt. There it stays milky grey-green and then, over twelve seconds, shadows surface first, warm tones follow, and finally a handwritten caption appears on the border. Each of the eight frames is a tiny flat illustration in a faded-film palette: a striped parasol, a cat's back at a window, a boiled egg with steaming coffee, a caravan under pines, a bicycle, a lighthouse with a breathing beam, a cake with flickering candles, two feet at the end of a towel. The counter runs from 8 to 0, the shutter goes grey under an "empty" tag, and a sticker on the film box loads a fresh pack. There is not a line of script on the page.

tags: - Whole state machine in CSS: eight checkboxes tied to an empty form, stacked labels over the shutter, :has(:checked) selectors, and a delayed visibility animation that re-arms the button only after the motor stops - Re-triggering one-shot effects (flash, bloom, iris, recoil, counter roll, "whirrr") by alternating twin keyframe names through custom properties on each state - Print ejection as one keyframe animation with per-segment timing: steps() for the motor, clip-path inset synchronised with the translate so the print is revealed at the slot line, then eased drop and glide to variable-driven coordinates and rotation - Twelve-second development using animated opacity plus a grayscale/sepia/saturate/contrast/brightness filter chain and a fading milky radial overlay; caption revealed with an animated clip-path - Eight 1:1 illustrations built only from positioned boxes, border-radius, conic/repeating/radial gradients, clip-path polygons and multi box-shadows, on a 100-unit em grid so they scale with the print - Camera drawn from divs: nested lens rings, conic iris blades with a radial mask, ribbed flash diffuser, knurled dial, counter window fed by a CSS counter decremented by each checked input - Woven strap from a thick bordered ellipse with dashed stitching and a masked repeating-conic weave - Flat stacked box-shadows for soft long shadows, diagonal window-light gradients and a turbulence grain over the blush table - Fixed-proportion stage sized from one viewport-derived unit, with a second coordinate set for phones and portrait screens - Reduced-motion variant with no flash, recoil or flight: prints simply appear in place, developed and captioned

notes.zh: 作者自述：A dark room, a single moulded terminal, and an amber tube that warms from a bright line into a full raster, counts its memory, draws its own banner and then builds a greenhouse dashboard frame by frame. Everything on the glass is a character in an exact 80-column grid: bars, sparklines, a plumbing diagram with arrows creeping through the pipes, a solar array that silts up cell by cell, and six planter beds whose potatoes, wheat, lettuce, soy, radishes and one sunflower called Gerald sprout, sway, droop when thirsty and ripen while you watch. The station runs itself with a dry sense of humour until a dust storm rolls in, the screen dims, an orange alarm flashes and the machine starts switching off lamps, Gerald's first; the viewer, standing in for Dr. Imani Okoro-Lindqvist on sol 412 of a solitary posting, decides what stays lit. The log alternates terse system lines with her notes, and the wall beside the terminal quietly holds 412 tally marks.

tags: - Character-cell screen buffer (80x39 or 40x41) composed every frame and diffed row by row into DOM text, with non-ASCII glyphs locked to one-cell boxes so box-drawing, block and symbol characters stay on the grid - Font size solved from the measured glyph advance so the column count always fits the tube exactly; interactive hit zones are transparent buttons laid over cell rectangles - Phosphor bloom from layered amber text-shadows, inverse-video cells, a mid and dim intensity level, and hot orange reserved for alarms, shed loads and the cursor - Phosphor persistence: every changed numeric cell leaves a blurred ghost of its old characters that decays over three quarters of a second - CRT glass built in CSS: scanline overlay, slow rolling refresh band, irregular flicker, vignette and inner shadow for curvature, a corner highlight, power-save dimming, and a warm-up beam that expands from a line to the full raster - Boot choreography on a wall-clock timeline: memory count, block-letter banner, panel frames traced character by character behind an orange drawing head - Procedural and hand-drawn plant sprites per growth stage with per-row sway offsets, a droop transform (leaves flip, heads nod, the plant sinks), soil texture mapped to moisture, roots and tubers drawn into the soil row - Particle cascade in character cells for the harvest, with a typed inverse-video yield tag - Block-element data graphics: half-block bars, auto-scaled sparklines, a two-row insolation curve, dust drawn as shaded cells on the array with a sweeping brush - Row-shift glitches and faster flicker while a storm is overhead - Moulded bezel with turbulence grain, embossed nameplate, vent slots and a power LED that turns orange and pulses in power-save - Seeded hand-jittered SVG tally marks on the wall, exactly 412 - Square-wave and filtered-noise sound synthesised with Web Audio, created only after the sound key is used

notes.zh: 作者自述：A complete broadsheet front page for an invented port city, printed in ink black on yellowing newsprint: a blackletter nameplate with an engraved harbour vignette, weather and price ears, a ruled dateline, and seven columns of period journalism about a great fog, a new electric tramway, an escaped circus sea-lion, a police court, a serial story, shipping, sport and small advertisements whose details quietly refer to one another. On arrival a press cylinder's shadow rolls down the sheet and the ink lands block by block; the three press photographs are true halftones that can be examined dot by dot under a brass loupe. The paper carries grain, a centre fold, uneven impression and the ghost of page two showing through, and it reflows to three columns on tablets and a dense single-column "late extra" on phones.

tags: - Blackletter nameplate generated as SVG by sweeping a broad-nib pen (fixed 38° angle) along hand-plotted stroke skeletons, giving authentic thick and thin strokes - Hand-drawn inline SVG engravings: harbour vignette with lighthouse, steamer and gulls; isobar chart; tonic bottle; sou'westered fisherman; printer's fist - Procedural greyscale scenes painted on an offscreen canvas (fog-bound steamer and crane, hats at the tram depot, sea-lion on a marble slab) and converted to a real 45° amplitude-modulated halftone screen with dot gain, jittered registration and uneven impression - Loupe canvas that re-screens the photograph at 4x with rough-edged dots and paper fibres, inside a conic-gradient brass rim - Condensed headline type made from bold serif capitals compressed horizontally, sized with container query units; multi-deck headlines alternating capitals and italics with centred dashes - CSS grid broadsheet layout with hairline column rules, multi-column justified body text with soft hyphens, cross-heads kept with their paragraphs, dotted leaders in tabular lists - Paper texture from a generated grain tile, edge yellowing gradients, horizontal and vertical fold creases, mirrored show-through type at about 3% opacity, per-column ink opacity and a faint ink-spread shadow - Press-run animation: a cylinder shadow sweeps the viewport while each block is revealed by a clip-path wipe timed to its position, staggered left to right - Hinged 3D unfold of a newsprint reading panel with its own crease - Pencil underline drawn across wrapped lines with an animated background, and hand-wobbled SVG rings drawn with stroke-dash animation

notes.zh: 作者自述：A hot-pink colour field with an oversized halftone and a glossy plate, onto which the word WOBBLE drops letter by letter as soon as the page opens: fat, translucent lemon, lime, blue-raspberry and orange jellies that squash to two-thirds of their height, bulge into each other, rebound and keep quivering. Every glyph is a hand-drawn chunky outline turned into a real soft body, so everything the viewer types, drags, pokes or flings behaves like gelatine: highlights stretch as the shape deforms, bubbles ride along inside, coloured light pools on the plate underneath. The page is a toy with almost no chrome: a tiny label, four jelly-cube flavour swatches, three round grape buttons, a candy-wrapper text field and a row of wrapped sweets that drop sample words.

tags: - Custom chunky outline font (41 glyphs with counters) defined as polygons, corner-rounded and resampled into boundary point masses - Soft-body simulation: verlet integration at 120 Hz, shape matching with area-preserving linear blend, ring/bend/cross-bracing springs, viscous damping and soft terminal velocity - Point-versus-polygon collisions between letters with sticky floor friction and an ooze-through untangling mode - Catmull-Rom smoothed outlines filled with translucent vertical gradients on Canvas 2D - Clipped inner rim strokes, plus specular and pooled-light ribbons rebuilt every frame from live surface normals so they stretch with the jelly - Glints anchored to boundary points and bubbles skinned to their nearest outline points - Flavour-tinted caustic glows and grape contact shadows on the plate, computed from what is actually touching - Pre-rendered backdrop canvas: large rotated halftone with size gradient and layered ellipse plates - Droplet bursts and expanding rings for pops and pokes - CSS-drawn jelly cubes, wrapped candies (clip-path twists) and a pinking-sheared candy-wrapper input, with springy cubic-bezier hover and press states - Synthesised blop, pop, slurp and thud sounds with Web Audio, pitched by letter size

notes.zh: 作者自述：A single sheet from an imagined eighteenth-century astronomical atlas, lit as if by a candle: laid paper with chain lines, grain and foxing, a border of tiny asterisks, and a title cartouche set in mixed capitals, small caps and italic. At its centre sits an embossed plate-mark holding a graduated degree circle, an engraved radiant Sun, and two small planets circling at their true relative speeds. Every few days a hair-fine line is ruled between them and left behind; within three seconds the first petal appears, and over eight simulated years the tangle resolves into the five-petalled rose of the 13 : 8 near-resonance. When the cycle closes a red flourish draws itself under the caption, asterisks mark the five conjunction points, and the caption states plainly how far the figure misses closure. Left alone, the next eight years are then ruled slowly in madder red over the first, a hair askew. The viewer can change pace, weave density and view, scrub through time, and swap in five other planetary pairs, each with its ratio and loop count worked out from the same twelve numbers. A short two-column essay insists, calmly, that it is all only division.

tags: - Canvas line accumulation at very low alpha with per-line jitter of weight and opacity, so dense regions darken like cross-hatching; a second canvas layer for the red re-drawing - Inline SVG instruments over the canvas: degree ring with 360 generated ticks, orbit circles ticked by stroke-dasharray, engraved Sun, compass rose, planets, live chord, scrub hairline - SVG textPath labels curved along the orbits, with paper-coloured halos so they stay legible over the weave - feTurbulence paper grain and foxing, feDisplacementMap wobble on engraved linework for ink irregularity - CSS laid-paper chain lines, inset-shadow plate-mark emboss, flickering candle vignette - Star border from an SVG pattern of six-armed asterisks with drawn corner stars - Engraved title typography in Baskerville-family system serifs with old-style numerals, small caps, drop cap and justified narrow columns - SVG swash flourishes drawn in by stroke-dashoffset; spring-eased marks, knob and thumbnail motion - Procedurally built year ruler (alternating scale bar, ticks, numerals) rebuilt for each pair and width - Continued-fraction computation of the nearest simple period ratio, loop count and closure error for each pair - Thumbnails rendered by the same drawing routine as the main plate, in whichever view is active

notes.zh: 作者自述：A weathered slab of slate lies on dark ground, lit from the upper left, with a hairline crack, stepped cleavage and two rust veins. Three lichen colonies are already growing on it when the page opens: a mustard crust branching into coral lobes, a sage shield lichen unrolling broad leafy lobes, and a chalk-white crust budding at its edge. They grow slowly but visibly, with pale young margins, raised relief and soft shadows; their centres age, darken, crack and break out in tiny dark-rimmed fruiting discs. When colonies meet they stop and hold a thin black frontier, and over a century the slab turns into a map of territories. A pinned field card in a typewriter face and italic hand records the year and each species' share of the stone; a specimen tray offers four species to sow; a brass hand lens follows the pointer and magnifies the crust two and a half times. The mood is quiet, damp and northern.

tags: - Gray-Scott reaction–diffusion in WebGL 2 on ping-pong float framebuffers, with a nine-point Laplacian and several iterations per frame - Species-id and colonisation-time channels: per-species feed/kill/diffusion/rate, claiming of bare stone, no-flux territory borders - Moisture field (drifting noise plus the crack) modulating local reaction rate; rain raises it everywhere - Procedural slate: fbm height, anisotropic cleavage lines, stepped terraces, crack groove, rust veins, baked to a normal/tone texture - Signed-distance slab outline with chipped corners, bevel light and a ground shadow - Lichen shading from the chemical field: gradient normals, cast shadow, damp halo, pale young margin, age darkening, growth rings from colonisation time - Voronoi areole cracking and hashed apothecia with rims in old crust; manual bilinear blending of species colours and a drawn contact line - Wet look: darkened albedo, specular sheen, animated drop rings - Hand lens: in-shader 2.5× magnification with slight barrel distortion and extra procedural detail, under a CSS conic-gradient brass rim and handle - Slate-knife wipe rendered in the shader with blade, shadow and dust streaks - Field card in CSS: ruled paper, margin line, SVG turbulence grain, drawing-pin, self-typing typewriter title, hand-inked tick, ruler slider, stamped buttons - Specimen swatches drawn in inline SVG with turbulence displacement - Asynchronous coverage readback through a pixel-pack buffer and fence sync - Canvas 2D reaction–diffusion fallback and a reduced-motion still that advances by decades

notes.zh: 作者自述：The page is the decorated surface of an Attic black-figure drinking cup: a terracotta ground with clay grain, wheel marks, hairline cracks and a chipped rim, black glaze bands carrying the title in spaced, slightly uneven cream capitals, a Greek-key meander above and below, a running-wave band, and two palmettes flanking a round tondo. Inside the tondo is a freshly generated ring labyrinth. A small black silhouette of Theseus steps in at the gate paying out an oxide-red thread that lies along the corridor floors with a little slack; Asterion sleeps in the central chamber under his own name. Reaching him wakes him, the meanders begin to scroll, and the way out is the thread itself, rewound step by step while the Minotaur pathfinds behind, stopping to sniff at junctions. Escape sends the whole thread springing back along the remembered route, pulling taut, lifting off the pot and winding into a ball on the cream roundel beside the title while the vessel makes one slow turn and a cream slip panel delivers the inscription.

tags: - Polar maze on concentric rings (cell counts doubling outward) generated by seeded depth-first search with added loops; breadth-first pathfinding for the pursuer - Canvas 2D rendering of walls as arcs and radials, batched into five opacity "glazes" for the fog of memory, with a thin cream sheen pass on the black - Thread as a polyline sampled in polar space, Chaikin-smoothed at corners, with arclength-keyed slack that settles in behind the walker and is cut precisely on retrace; cream edge, drop shadow and twist dashes - Finale on a full-viewport overlay canvas: resampled thread morphs from the maze path to a taut line with a lifting shadow, then reels into a parametric ball of thread - Black-figure silhouettes drawn procedurally with a terracotta halo and cream incised lines, two-frame walk, facing by direction of travel; names lettered along arcs - Inline SVG patterns for the Greek-key meander and running wave, scrolled by pattern transforms; SVG palmette symbol; circular meander generated for the touch disc - Procedural clay grain and wheel-mark tile painted at load, SVG hairline cracks and a chipped rim, gradient sheen and vessel-curvature shading - Clip-path brush wipes for the bands, centre-outward wall draw-in, staggered per-letter inscription reveal, custom cubic-bezier easings - Web Audio frame drum (pitched sine drop plus filtered noise) whose tempo follows the Minotaur's distance, and lyre-like plucked tones

notes.zh: 作者自述：A long-scroll specimen for Halden Grotesk, an invented geometric grotesk from the invented foundry Nordre Type, in which no font file exists: all 35 glyphs are stored in the page as explicit on-curve and off-curve points and drawn from that data. The page is clinical and Scandinavian: specimen-paper off-white, black, and a single cobalt used for construction lines, points and one giant letter, organised on a twelve-column grid with hairline rules and mono section numbers. The cover crops an enormous "Halden" at the viewport edges and assembles it from points, outline and a rising flood of ink. Anatomy pins one glyph out on a metrics grid with every coordinate labelled and every point draggable; because that drawing is the master, damaging the "a" damages every "a" on the page until it is reset. Construction shows the compass work behind O, G and D and an eight-times vertical exaggeration of the overshoot; In use sets a waterfall, a weight row, a poster and ferry-terminal signage from the drawn letters only; Spacing lets the viewer kern a pair by hand until it snaps to the foundry's value; the Colophon carries the designer's note, a licensing joke and the full character grid with its gaps.

tags: - Hand-authored glyph outlines (lines and cubic beziers, 1000 units per em) parsed into a shared point model that renders fill, outline, handles and points from the same data - Inline SVG text setting with a kerning table, per-word wrapping and size control through a single CSS variable - Three global rendering modes (ink, outline, x-ray) switched by a root attribute; x-ray overlays are built lazily as compact zero-length-stroke point paths so hundreds of glyphs stay cheap - Staged drawing sequence: points appear in order with ticking coordinate labels, handles extend, contours stroke on with stroke-dashoffset, fill floods upward with a clip-path wipe - Metrics grid with baseline, x-height, cap height, ascender, descender, side bearings and advance, lines extending from the margins - Greedy label collision thinning and screen-constant point and stroke sizes via a per-SVG units-per-pixel variable - Construction circles and tangents drawn in cobalt and inverted to paper where they cross the black glyph, using the glyph itself as a clip path - Broken-view overshoot diagram with non-uniform vertical scaling - Faux bold weight by outline expansion; flat cobalt poster and black signage panel with drawn arrows - Hatched character grid distinguishing drawn from undrawn glyphs; reduced-motion variant with all glyphs complete

notes.zh: 作者自述：A single woodblock print hangs on a pale wall and quietly lives. An arched timber bridge runs in a long diagonal from a snowbank and its reeds to a far shore of thatched and tiled houses, a stone lantern and two cinnabar gate posts, under one snow-capped mountain that dissolves into the sky. Everything is cut as a printer would cut it: flat colour blocks with woodgrain showing through, hand-wiped bokashi at the top of the sky and along the water's edge, dark indigo keyblock lines whose width breathes, colour sitting a hair out of register, and snow that is simply unprinted paper. On arrival the sheet is pulled block by block (sky, water, greys, red, key lines), the cartouche settles and the two artist seals are stamped last. Then snow falls in three depths, wave lines drift down the river, a figure in a straw cape under a red umbrella crosses the bridge with a dog or a lantern-bearer behind, chimney smoke curls, crows pass now and then, a roof sheds its load. The hour follows the viewer's clock; pressing the round seal re-inks the sky from the top down, and at dusk the windows and lanterns come on one after another, their light laid on the river as short warm strokes. On phones the scene recomposes as a tall oban sheet; on wide screens it is a diptych.

tags: - Canvas 2D scene cut into separate "blocks" (sky, water, greys, red, keyblock) that are composited with small per-block offsets for visible misregistration - Keyblock lines drawn as thin filled shapes with noise-modulated width, wandering path and tapered ends rather than uniform strokes - Procedural woodgrain (long wavy parallel streaks bending around knots) applied as a pattern inside every printed flat; snow areas left as bare paper - Bokashi gradation built from a tiny per-column sky strip, so the hand-wiped edge is slightly uneven and can be re-inked with a soft top-down wipe - Layered edge washes along shorelines for the darker band at the water's edge and blue shadow on snow - Occlusion by carving: every opaque shape erases the key and red blocks beneath it, like cutting away wood - Two full compositions (portrait oban and landscape diptych) generated from one set of parametric drawing routines - Three-depth snowfall of flat off-white dots, the farthest layer passing behind houses and bridge - Walker, lantern traveller, dog and crows as flat silhouettes with simple walk and wing cycles; the walker passes behind the near bridge rail, which is cut on its own block - Pine bough on its own block, rotated on a damped spring; each snow load is a separate sprite that can fall and burst - A single multiply overprint for the hour, with lamplight (the only warm ink) and its river reflections drawn afterwards - Paper fibre overlay across sheet and margins, SVG turbulence filters for the worn cinnabar seals - Entrance choreography in printing order, with the cartouche and seals stamped at the end - Optional synthesised sound: filtered-noise wind that follows the gusts and soft snow creaks on each footstep

notes.zh: 作者自述：A jeweller's-black landing page whose hero is a working watch. The Heure Bleue 38 lies caseback-up beside a large Didone title: under the sapphire, a ruthenium-dark calibre with rose-gold wheels is actually running, every wheel meshing at its true ratio and the whole train stepping six times a second to the viewer's own local time. In the first three seconds the crown turns three clicks, the ratchet advances, the blued mainspring tightens in the barrel, and the balance kicks into life. Turning the watch over reveals a restrained ivory dial with applied gold indices, blued leaf hands, small seconds at six and a moon-shaped power reserve; everything on both faces is annotated in French and English on hover or tap. Below, four sparse sections ruled in thin gold give the specifications, the two-person workshop, three finishing close-ups that respond to light, and a waiting list whose confirmation is engraved letter by letter onto a caseback ring.

tags: - Inline SVG calibre generated from tooth counts: ogival involute-like gear outlines, spoked wheels, steel pinions, wolf-tooth ratchet, club-tooth escape wheel, pallet fork with ruby pallets, all placed from computed centre distances - One clock derived from Date.now(): mesh-phase formula keeps every tooth in its gap; the escape wheel advances 12 degrees per beat, unlocked by a fork whose angle is driven by the balance's own angle - Hairspring redrawn each frame as an Archimedean spiral whose inner end follows the balance, so the coils breathe; mainspring spiral that clusters toward the arbor as the reserve rises - Côtes de Genève as a rotated repeating gradient pattern on stroke-built bridges with bevelled (anglage) edges; perlage as an overlapping-circle pattern on the mainplate; engraved capitals set on arcs with textPath - Gold rendered with radial gradients plus fixed-angle sheen rings that stay still while the wheels turn; case, bezel and waiting-list ring in CSS conic gradients; jewels in gold chatons; heat-blued screws with slots at varied angles - 3D case: preserve-3d flip of two back-face-hidden faces, lugs, strap and knurled crown, with pointer-driven tilt and a drifting sapphire reflection - Ivory dial with grain (feTurbulence), railroad minute track, faceted applied indices, two-tone leaf hands with offset shadows, crescent power-reserve filled through a clip path - Staggered entrance with a custom cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.1,1), hairline rules that draw themselves, film-grain overlay - Finishing vignettes whose gradients are re-aimed by pointer position: a bevel that flashes, a black-polished screw that is black from every angle but one, a light pooling across perlage - Synthesised tick/tock (band-passed noise bursts, alternating timbre) and ratchet clicks through Web Audio, off by default - Reduced-motion mode: gears and balance are posed correctly but still; only the hands and the time readout update once per second

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sunlit sewing table seen from above: a beech embroidery hoop with a brass screw holds a square of cream aida cloth, and on it a small sampler stitches itself in over the first three seconds while a steel needle darts from stitch to stitch. Everything the viewer places is rendered as real thread: two crossed strands of twisted floss with sheen, shadow and hand-made irregularity, pulled from hole to hole with a little tightening bounce. To the left sit a stitched fabric title label, a wooden sewing-box tray of tools, ten bobbin cards of floss and a library of stamped motifs with a "stitch these words" field; to the right a paper pattern card keeps the project name, floss usage in metres, finished size and time. The hoop can be turned over in 3D to reveal the honest, messy back of the work, computed from the true sewing order, or swapped for a printable symbol chart with a key.

tags: - Layered 2D canvas scene: procedurally woven aida tile (thread bundles, corner holes), grain noise, slack darker cloth with folds and a stitched hem outside the hoop - Each stitch drawn as shaded strands: dark edge, floss body, slanted twist plies, off-centre sheen, drop shadow, crossing shadow, seeded jitter and thickness variation - Thread-pull animation per strand: eased draw from hole to hole, sagging and fat while loose, then a damped tightening bounce - Wooden hoop with gradient lighting, concentric grain arcs, bevels, cast shadow, split lugs and a knurled brass screw - Reverse side generated from the actual stitch order: short travelling stitches, sagging long carries, knots with tails and frayed loose ends, mirrored - 3D flip of the whole hoop with a perspective transform and an overshooting settle; cross-fade under reduced motion - Symbol chart drawn to canvas: tinted cells, one symbol per floss, bold tens, centre arrows, backstitch lines and a generated key - Title lettered in real cross-stitch from the page's own 5x7 alphabet on a pinked fabric label pinned with brass pins - Tools drawn as inline SVG objects in a CSS wooden tray; floss as CSS bobbin cards; running-stitch dashed borders as the interface motif - Linen table texture and a soft-light window-light overlay; canvas toBlob export of the hoop as a PNG

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sunlit natural-history gallery wall in shell-pink plaster. A large porcelain-white shell floats above a linen-covered drum that stands on a pale cabinet of eight brass-labelled drawers; beside it hang a paper museum label and a brass-and-ivory instrument of five sliders and two rows of small specimen trays. On arrival a chambered nautilus grows out of its own apex, whorl after whorl, flame stripes and all. Pulling a drawer makes that shell become another before the visitor's eyes: the flat coil tightens and telescopes into a turret, swells into a cone shell tiled with computed tents, or flares open into a ribbed cockle valve, while the label re-sets itself, the slider handles slide to their new places and a crosshair travels across the map of all possible shells below. Sawing the nautilus open reveals a spiral of pearly chambers. The tone is quiet scholarship: classical serif titles, tracked small-cap legends, plain accurate copy about why a shell that grows only at its edge must be a logarithmic spiral, and how David Raup found that life uses only part of the space the equation allows.

tags: - Software 3D on Canvas 2D: a swept-ellipse mesh (up to about 16,000 quads) rebuilt into preallocated typed arrays, perspective projection, bucket-sorted painter's algorithm - Raup-style coiling model with adaptive, per-half-whorl step distribution, tapered protoconch and analytic removal of wall buried inside earlier whorls - Per-quad lighting in model space: wrapped diffuse with warm shadow tint, tight specular for a porcelain surface, depth-darkened pink interior, optional iridescent nacre - Geometric ornament (spiral cords, axial ribs, shoulder knobs) by displacing the generating curve; growth lines as fine alternating tint - Pigment computed in surface parameter space with 2×2 supersampling: flames, spiral bands, dots, and a tent pattern from an excitable one-dimensional cellular automaton drawn at twice the mesh resolution by splitting quads - Two section modes with real cut faces: axial saw for spired shells, median saw for flat coils, plus dished septa with thickened cut edges - Eased interpolation of every parameter, ornament and pigment weight, and quaternion slerp of the view, so presets morph continuously - Growth entrance by extending the sweep from apex to aperture against a fixed final frame - Morphospace chart on canvas: warped log axis, tinted and hatched regions, about sixty miniature shells rendered by the same engine at their own coordinates, crosshair, dotted trail - Procedural linen plinth with weave pattern and soft elliptical shadow that follows the lamp - CSS craft: skewed, blurred window-light with mullions drifting across the wall, feTurbulence paper grain, brass-and-ivory range sliders, engraved drawer fronts with brass label frames and knobs, letterpress-style label re-set animation, masked title entrance

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sideways journey down an invented English river, drawn as one continuous flat-colour panorama in the manner of a children's atlas for grown-ups. The page opens in rain on a moor, with the title lettered large in rough-edged Palatino italic and a paper boat dropping into a spring no wider than a pencil line. Scrolling carries the reader 138 kilometres downstream: over a gritstone fall, under a packhorse bridge, past a turning mill wheel, through buttercup meadows, a terraced brewery town, a working lock, pylons and poplars, mudflats, docks, and finally past a lighthouse into an evening sea. The river is a single unbroken blue path that widens from a thread to the whole lower third of the stage, and the little boat rides it the entire way, behaving differently at every obstacle. Each of the eleven stations carries a white-on-green kilometre sign and a short, dry caption; a slim strip along the bottom shows the whole river in miniature with an altitude profile and a live readout of distance, height and flow.

tags: - One viewport-sized inline SVG whose layer groups are translated at different rates (distant fells 0.18, rolling country 0.4, clouds 0.22, river and banks 1, foreground reeds, fences and railings 1.5) from a single eased camera value driven by vertical scroll in a tall track with a sticky stage - Geometry computed in the page: cosine-interpolated river centreline, width and ground-line functions produce the river polygon, banks, bank hachures, hedged field patchwork, far ridgelines and the minimap from the same data - Strict five-colour palette with tints mixed in code; consistent 3-unit ink outlines; texture from SVG hatch, brick, dot, grass and buttercup patterns; gradients used only in the river and sea - Flowing water as dashed flow lines per reach whose dash-offset speed and dash length follow the gradient (fast and white at the fall, long and slow in the estuary), plus an animated fall, weir, mill race and surf line - Scroll-linked lock choreography: chamber water level, mitre gates, the narrowboat's rise and exit, and the paper boat's wait, entry and descent are all functions of camera position, with the camera slowed through that stretch - Paper boat behaviour model: follows the river slope, tumbles through 360 degrees over the fall, spins in the mill race, jolts over the weir, sidesteps the rowing eight, bobs harder at sea, and drifts on into a circling eddy when scrolling stops - Weather and light along the journey: animated rain pattern and hatched storm clouds on the moor, a rayed sun over the meadows, sky colour interpolated to a buttercup evening, a setting sun with a glitter path on a sea that the river's fill fades into - Approach-triggered birds (curlew, dipper, heron, waders, gulls, wagtails) with two-frame wing animation; turning water wheel, luffing cranes, crossing ferry, chimney smoke, rocking buoys, a pulsing lighthouse lamp - Hand-lettered map labels on curves with SVG textPath; a turbulence displacement filter roughens the title and end line; a fine paper grain overlay - HTML captions and title travelling with the landscape; group culling of off-screen scenes; reduced-motion mode that snaps between stations

notes.zh: 作者自述：A black acrylic desk toy fills the viewport: a glossy rounded frame slung between two chrome posts, holding roughly ten thousand hexagonally packed steel pin-heads (about five thousand on a phone). On arrival a hand presses in from behind and withdraws, and its impression slowly melts back into the lattice. Every pin is a tiny domed, lathe-turned disc lit by a single raking lamp, so slopes facing the light flash white, slopes facing away drop to dark steel and raised forms throw shadows across their lower neighbours. The pointer itself becomes a hand pushing through the field; dragging leaves a subsiding trail. A tray of machined black keys presses in a hand, a mask-like face, a sphere, a travelling ripple, a typed word and the current time, and a flip key tips the frame so the whole field cascades out and back in a glittering wave. The only colour anywhere is one thin red line on the brushed-steel logo plate, which states the true pin count.

tags: - WebGL point-sprite renderer: one point per pin, round heads cut and antialiased in the fragment shader, with a Canvas 2D fallback using pre-rendered disc sprites in 16 brightness levels - Per-fragment lighting on each pin-head: surface normal from the neighbouring pin heights plus a small dome, diffuse and tight specular terms, a bow-tie "turned steel" glint aimed at the lamp, darkened chamfer rim, per-pin brightness variance - Height-field gradients computed on the hexagonal lattice by least squares over the six neighbours; cast shadows found by marching four steps toward the lamp - Height-dependent parallax and 15% growth of raised heads, with a perspective-varying parallax vector so the field reads as slightly tilted - Steel tone ramp restricted to #0B0C0E, #6C7480, #C9CED6 and #FFFFFF, plus a lamp-centred sheen falloff across the flat lattice - Spring-and-gravity pin physics in typed arrays: fast underdamped spring when pushed, slow friction-limited relaxation with slightly randomised rates when released, bouncing free-fall during the flip - Procedural height maps: capsule-and-ellipsoid hand, ellipsoid mask face, sphere, animated concentric wave, and text rasterised offscreen then box-blurred per pin - CSS-built object: acrylic frame with lamp-tracked gloss, chrome cylinder posts with knurled caps and pivots, brushed-steel plate with slotted screws, floor glow, film grain - Frame swing on a hand-written spring driving a 3D rotateX under perspective - Inline SVG icons for the tray, lamp and hint; tracked small-caps geometric sans typography - Synthesised sound: a looped buffer of thousands of tiny decaying noise ticks through two band-pass filters, gain driven by the summed pin velocity - Idle detection (nothing is simulated or redrawn when the field is at rest), DPR capped at 2, frame-time measurement that thins the lattice on slow machines

title.zh: BÉTON BRUT — Six Buildings Nobody Asked For
title.en: BÉTON BRUT — Six Buildings Nobody Asked For

notes.zh: 作者自述：A photocopied architecture zine, issue six of BÉTON BRUT, laid out as nine full-viewport spreads on a board-marked concrete-grey ground. Colossal condensed capitals crop at the page edges and run behind six isometric concrete models of an invented new town, Northmere; typewritten essays by the zine-maker Dot Ferreira sit on taped-down pale slips with orange marginal numbering. As each spread arrives its building is poured storey by storey out of the base plate, flashing orange formwork as each lift sets, then the giant name slams in behind it, the page shakes and a rubber stamp lands. Every model can be turned, pulled apart into a labelled section and re-lit with a sun slider that throws a long shadow across the page. A charcoal manifesto spread and a back cover with a creased fold-out site plan and a cut-out subscription coupon close the issue. The tone is monumental, argumentative, affectionate and a bit funny.

tags: - Isometric models built from divs with CSS 3D transforms (preserve-3d, orthographic rotateX/rotateY rig): extruded boxes, many-sided drums, tilted folded plates with clipped gables, a 50-segment helical ramp - Per-face lighting computed from a sun vector: each face normal is dotted with the light direction and mapped onto a pale-cement to charcoal concrete ramp, with orange details shaded on their own ramp - Projected ground shadows: every volume's corners are projected along the sun vector onto the base plate, convex-hulled and drawn as one SVG path lying in the ground plane - Pour choreography with individual scale/translate properties, cubic-bezier(.7,0,.2,1), 250–400 ms lifts staggered by level, and a keyframed orange formwork outline that sets to concrete - Board-marked concrete from layered repeating gradients (plank lines, knots, tie-hole grids), water stains and moss as blurred gradient streaks, SVG turbulence grain - Photocopier grit: an SVG turbulence alpha mask punching toner dropouts into the giant type, page numerals and rubber stamps - Window modules drawn with tiled conic gradients so one face carries a whole grid of openings - Overprint: orange type and the cover sun set to multiply over charcoal letters - Billboarded scale figures, section labels and plan markers that counter-rotate to face the viewer inside the 3D rig - Fallback-font fitting: canvas text measurement drives a horizontal squeeze so any heavy grotesque matches the condensed display width - Crop marks, taped paper slips with hard offset shadows, fold creases on the site plan, dashed coupon border with SVG scissors, hand-drawn SVG signature that writes itself

notes.zh: 作者自述：A living four-colour screenprint. A cream sheet carries a giant stacked "sand / pile" title with misregistered orange and blue shadows, and the dot of its "i" is itself a seven-by-seven sandpile that never stops toppling. Beside it a large square table with a black outline and a hard shadow sits empty for half a second, then a tap opens over the centre and a fractal medallion of ink, orange and blue blooms outward behind a ragged yellow front before settling into a slow drip. Everything else on the sheet is a readout of that one rule: a looping four-panel pictogram, a legend whose bars and counts follow the table, a tally in tabular numerals, and a log-log plot whose orange points drop into place along a blue fitted line as random rain is measured. The viewer pours, pins taps, drops handfuls of ten thousand grains, computes the group identity, sweeps the table with a diagonal wipe and saves the result as a poster.

tags: - Abelian sandpile on Int32/Uint8 typed arrays with a sink border and a swapped pair of active lists, toppled in waves under a per-frame time budget - Palette-indexed Uint32 writes into ImageData on a grid-resolution canvas, scaled with image-rendering: pixelated - Flat yellow "overprint" tint that marks the footprint of each measured avalanche for a fixed number of frames - Procedurally generated paper grain tiled over the whole page with multiply blending - Title fitted to its column by measurement, with hard offset text shadows and a canvas sandpile positioned as the dot of the i from measured glyph metrics - SVG rule pictogram built from palette-coloured cells, cycling with phase-shifted keyframes and grains that fly to the neighbours - Log-binned histogram in SVG with decade grid, points that settle by eased transforms, and a least-squares power-law line with its slope - Diagonal wipes (sweep and critical loading) with eased ink front drawn into the pixel buffer - Identity element computed live in two animated stabilisations - Flat chip controls with black outlines and hard shadows that depress on press; custom range slider; blue focus rings - PNG export of the field by nearest-neighbour upscaling

title.zh: Seven Sisters — A Nest of Dolls
title.en: Seven Sisters — A Nest of Dolls

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sheet of cream paper with a folk-painted shelf across its lower third, a slowly turning floral rosette behind it, and one lacquered nesting doll standing in the middle. Tap her at the waist and her top half springs up, tips and is set down leaning on the shelf, a dark wooden hollow appears, and the next sister rises out of it, hops over the rim, lands with a squash and a wobble, and gets her name ribbon; the row slides to stay centred as the family grows. Six times this repeats, each sister smaller by a fifth and painted with her own scarf, face and apron motif (sunflower, strawberries, rooster, samovar, rowan, tulip), until Little Zoya, who is solid and asleep. Tapping Zoya wakes her: her eyes open, she blushes and jumps, the painted bird leaves her apron, grows as it climbs and circles above the sisters, and seventeen flowers bloom one by one along the bottom border. All of it runs without a single line of script.

tags: - Seven checkboxes and general-sibling selector chains as the only state machine; a doll is open only when she and all her elders are checked - Recursively nested dolls sized in their own em, so one font-size rule gives the constant 0.8 ratio and stacking order (hollow, inner doll, front wall, lid) is correct at every depth - State passed down the nest through inherited custom properties that drive calc() transforms, transition delays, z-index, visibility and even animation names - Doll halves cut with matching clip-path polygons along an elliptical seam, with a curved waist band, wooden lip and dark radial-gradient hollow - Lid choreography split over four nested wrappers (lift on a spring curve, slide, drop, tilt) so each axis has its own easing and delay in both directions - Multi-stage hop keyframes with squash, rebound and a decaying wobble; a separate hop-back for closing - Faces, scarves, knots and six apron motifs built from border-radius shapes, rotated petals, gradients and multi-box-shadow clusters - Lacquer gloss streaks from soft radial gradients, contact shadows, polka-dot scarf patterns from layered radial gradients - Shelf and garden borders drawn entirely with repeating linear and radial gradients (diamonds, dots, leaves, scallops) - Rosette from repeating conic gradients, radial masks and dotted circular borders, rotating once every six minutes - Bird flight as two phase-shifted sine-eased axis animations (an ellipse with depth scaling and a direction flip), preceded by a climb that scales it up from apron size - CSS counters and custom-property strings for the live "n of 7 sisters are out" line and its changing hint - Paper grain from speckle gradients; full reduced-motion variant with opacity-only changes

notes.zh: 作者自述：A working observatory instrument presented as a page of stationery: an engraved masthead, a slate-and-brass elevation drawing of the seismograph (clockwork gearbox with a stepping escapement, a paper-wrapped drum sliding along its lead screw, long boom, knife-edge pivot, oil damper, sprung mass) and beneath it the unrolled recording sheet, where a simulated pen draws a continuous trace line by line. The page opens with the pen dropping onto the drum in the decaying surface waves of a distant earthquake, whose P, S and L flags, distance, magnitude nomogram, telegram and ledger entry appear as the first seconds pass. Everything the visitor does to the page (knocking, shaking, striking the pier with the mallet) is recorded by the same damped pen, annotated in red ink on the sheet and entered in the ledger with a dry remark. Analog readouts, a rack of filed sheets and a framed notice complete the bench.

tags: - Canvas seismogram with cached completed lines, a live line, red time-marker lifts, phase flags with hairlines, rotated handwritten annotations and a procedural paper grain - Fixed-step simulation of a driven damped oscillator (pen) with stops that clip to a flat-topped trace - Deterministic signal model: band-limited microseisms with slow sea-state swells plus seeded teleseisms (P onset, S, dispersed surface waves, coda) scheduled from the real clock - Inline SVG elevation animated per frame: the drum's rings show the actual recent trace wrapped round the cylinder, the seam turns with the drum, the drum creeps along its lead screw, the boom, stylus, spring and damper vane move with the pen - Stepping brass escapement and gear train with spring-eased beats - SVG analog readouts: 24-hour dial, station-noise needle gauge, drum-speed needle, dwindling paper roll, ink vial - Three-scale magnitude nomogram whose geometry really solves M = log A + 2.76 log D − 2.48, with an animated red isopleth - Typewriter telegram slip with perforated edge; ledger with tabular figures and ink-in row reveals - Paper-change choreography: the sheet lifts, is dated and initialled in script, shrinks into the rack as a thumbnail, and a fresh sheet wraps in - Page shudder driven by its own damped spring; expanding red ring at each knock; custom mallet cursor - Optional synthesized sound: escapement ticks, pen scratch following pen velocity, pier thumps, telegraph key clicks

notes.zh: 作者自述：A lamplit, velvet-dark room with one object in it: a bottle-green enamelled Holloway & Stern safe with gilt pinstriping, three brass hinges, a five-spoke handle and a large combination dial. After a filament flicker the lamp comes on and the dial gives one idle spin to zero. The viewer cracks a random three-number combination by intimacy with the mechanism rather than by reading a display: every graduation clicks, but the gate of the wheel being worked sounds lower, softer and doubled, the dial drags for an instant, the red index shivers and the needle of a small stethoscope gauge leaps. A notepad quietly pencils in each number when the viewer rests on it. Throwing the handle on a wrong setting gets a clunk and a shudder; on the right one the three bolts thud back one by one, the handle spins, and the heavy door swings open in true perspective, showing its thickness and boltwork, onto felt shelves holding one of five small stories: a pearl, a bundle of letters, a ship in a bottle, a sleeping cat, or a card that says "Too late. — M."

tags: - Layered inline SVG artwork for the safe frame, door, dial, handle, gauge, vault interior and five vault contents, all in the six-colour palette - Dial split into fixed and rotating layers: a rotating graduated band with 100 generated ticks, ivory numerals and a knurled brass ring, under fixed lighting gradients, with specular highlights and soft glints that travel across the domed knob as it turns - Real CSS 3D door: front face, back face with boltwork and an edge face with bolt ends, assembled with preserve-3d and swung on its hinge line with rotateY under perspective, using a slow heavy cubic-bezier ease - Bolt rods that slide inside clipped ports across the door seam into brass keepers on the jamb - Simulated three-wheel pack with pick-up play between wheels, gates, tolerances per grade and a false gate - Spring-damper needle physics for the stethoscope gauge, driven by impulses from clicks, gates and pick-ups - Web Audio synthesis: band-passed noise ticks, pitched-down double gate ticks, pick-up knocks, sub-bass bolt thunks, handle clunks, a resonant noise-sweep creak and a low room tone, with slight stereo panning by direction - SVG textPath gilt signwriting with block shading for the arched title and the maker's name - Lamp-pool lighting built from radial gradients, a corner vignette, faint striped wallpaper and feTurbulence grain; light spilling from the vault with a screen-blended glow - Paper, brass-plate and pencil textures in pure CSS: a typed card under a brass clip, a perforated ruled notepad with pencil write-in and rub-out animations, engraved plates with slotted screws - Entrance choreography: stepped filament flicker, then a decelerating idle spin of the dial - Reduced-motion variant: no flicker, spin, tremble or shudder, and the door opens with a cross-fade

notes.zh: 作者自述：A pale sunlight-yellow museum wall chart in Swiss information-design dress: a tight navy grotesk title, a serif-italic lede, tracked-caps labels and thin navy rules. The centrepiece is the daylight hourglass, a navy block of starry night with a sun-yellow band of day running through it, edged by orange, plum and blue twilight. On load the latitude sweeps from the equator to the Arctic Circle and settles on London, so the flat ribbon visibly swells into a lens. Beside it a small desk globe with a graduated meridian arc carries the latitude bead, the selected parallel and a terminator that tilts with the date, coloured with the same twilight bands as the chart. Above the chart the day length for the chosen date is set very large with its daily gain or loss, sunrise and sunset. Below, a heat map shows every latitude and day at once with labelled contours, a ring calendar bends the year into a sun-shaped figure, and a table of superlatives recalculates live. Everything is computed in the page from latitude and date.

tags: - Four canvases (hourglass chart, globe, heat map, ring calendar) drawn at device pixel ratio capped at 2 and redrawn only when state changes - Sunrise and twilight hour angles computed per half-day sample from solar declination, with clamping for polar day and polar night - Stacked band polygons for astronomical, nautical and civil twilight and daylight, with two-tone grid and solstice/equinox rules clipped to the day shape - Deterministic star field that only shows where the sun is more than 18° below the horizon - Edge-on orthographic globe with graticule, tilted terminator bands, subsolar sun glyph, two-tone latitude chord and a graduated meridian arc with tropic and polar-circle marks - Heat map rendered to an offscreen image from a 365 by 361 grid, with marching-squares contour lines at 6, 9, 12, 15 and 18 hours and pill labels - Ring calendar of 365 radial wedges with twilight bands, a dashed 12-hour reference circle and per-day rays - Custom cubic-bezier easing solved in script for latitude and date tweens, plus a choreographed intro sweep - Swiss typographic system: bold grotesk at extreme scale contrast, tabular numerals, tracked caps, serif italic annotations - Paper grain from an inline turbulence filter; staggered title and rule entrance animations

title.zh: The Drawloom — Cloth from a Diagram
title.en: The Drawloom — Cloth from a Diagram

notes.zh: 作者自述：A quiet linen-paper workshop page laid out as a classical weaving draft: threading on top, tie-up in the corner, treadling down the right, and a large cloth below that is computed entirely from those three grids. On arrival a wooden shuttle is already flying across an indigo warp, laying linen picks that the reed beats into goose-eye diamonds while the pressed treadle and lifted shafts glow gold in the diagram, making the cause-and-effect of the notation visible. Every thread is rendered as rounded, twisted yarn with highlights, dive-under shadows and looped selvedges, and a brass linen-tester lens enlarges the interlacement and warns in red of floats too long to wear. The left column holds the masthead, loom transport, generators, yarn choices and a plain-language reading of the weave; the right column is a pattern book of eight historical structures, each a tiny computed swatch.

tags: - Classical draft layout drawn on canvas with hairline, 4th and 8th-line grid weights, ink-square cells and tiny tabular edge figures - Procedural yarn rendering from cached sprites: rounded segments with cross-section gradients, twist streaks, end shadows where threads dive under, and continuous floats - Selvedge loops where the weft turns, bare hanging warp below the fell fading into a fringe - Pick-by-pick weaving animation: eased shuttle flight with trailing weft, reed swing, damped spring bounce of the cloth on each beat - Live highlighting of the active treadling row, tie-up column and lifted shafts in weld gold and madder - Back-eased ripple of grid cells when presets or generators rewrite the draft - 4× magnifier in a CSS brass frame (conic gradients, knurled ring, glass highlight) with red long-float warnings - Woven-paper page texture from layered CSS line gradients and generated grain - Pattern-book thumbnails computed from the same draft engine - Garamond-style serif masthead with small caps, tracked sans caps labels, custom shuttle-shaped slider thumb, ink-fill button hovers - Noise-burst synthesis for shaft clack and beater thump (off by default) - PNG export of the full swatch with typeset caption - Reduced-motion mode that renders the finished cloth without shuttle or entrance animation

notes.zh: 作者自述：A grey, overcast landing page for a fifth-generation umbrella maker on which it is actually raining: several hundred simulated drops fall in three depth layers across the whole viewport, splash on the top edges of the paper panels and the pavement, and blur and drain the colour from everything they fall on. The viewer holds the only bright thing on the page, a canary-yellow umbrella drawn in quarter view, which replaces the cursor. Rain bursts on its canopy, beads slide down the panels to the rib tips and fall in a steady drip, and beneath it a soft circle of the page is dry: sharp, full-contrast, and in colour. Reading the page means sheltering it. The copy is dry in the other sense: a headline that says it is raining in Garrow and usually is, an exploded drawing of the Garrow No. 4 that assembles itself when scrolled into view, a house catalogue of eleven grades of rain, a ruled price list for repairs, the shop's hours ("closed on dry days, i.e. the 3rd of August"), a note from Odalys Pluvia, and a footer wordmark standing at the edge of a puddle that reflects it upside-down and ripples when drops land.

tags: - Single full-viewport 2D canvas rain simulation on typed arrays: three depth layers of slanted streaks, wind sway, slow drizzle-to-downpour intensity cycle and occasional gusts - Arc collision of every drop against the umbrella's tilted canopy curve, spawning beads that travel along quadratic paths to the eight rib tips, which accumulate water and release it as falling drips - Splash crowns and perspective ripple rings where drops meet panel edges, the pavement line, the viewport floor and the footer puddle - Procedurally drawn umbrella (scalloped eight-panel canopy, ribs, ferrule, shaft, crook handle) with spring-lagged motion, velocity tilt and a parametric two-stage fold and pop-open - Wet/dry page split: a fixed backdrop-filter veil (blur, desaturation, lowered contrast) with canvas-generated running-water streak textures, pierced by a radial CSS mask tracked to the umbrella - Inline SVG exploded technical drawing with numbered callouts whose parts spring apart from the assembled position on entering view - Eleven small canvas vignettes, each a parametric rain pattern with a tiny yellow umbrella coping with it - SVG silhouette pedestrians with swinging legs and wet-pavement reflections walking past a tiled skyline, one umbrella yellow - Footer wordmark mirrored into a puddle through an animated feTurbulence and feDisplacementMap filter whose strength jumps when drops land - Fitted condensed grotesk headline type, tracked small-caps labels, Georgia body, tabular price figures; four-colour palette of rain grey, wet slate, canary yellow and dry white - Web Audio rain bed from filtered noise with a canopy patter that follows the measured hit rate

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sheet of green-bar fan-fold listing paper steps up out of a dark platen, a print head sweeps a JCL job banner and a huge "#" banner title across it, and then the rest of the sheet prints a seascape that will not hold still: a horizon, cloud wisps, a lighthouse on its rock, a little sailing boat, a bell buoy and a beach, every one of them made of typewriter characters and recomputed each frame from a perspective wave field in two ribbon colours, black for faces, crests and foam and sea-green for deep water. Moving the pointer is the weather: down for a glassy calm with mirror reflections, up for a gale with towering slashes, slanting rain, inverted-sheet lightning and a typed thunderclap, sideways for the wind. Whatever the viewer types falls from the sky into the water and rides the swell as a legible sentence, each letter on its own column of the wave, until it washes up as a tide line of their words. A footer in the voice of a shipping forecast for "Greenbar Bight" reprints itself in place as conditions change.
